nodes.description: Umbrella DO for UN-B2C85448 covering the provenance + audit-trail implementation surface. Components: libs/ner/span_resolver.py (character offsets, DI-B2512CB3), :Entity snippet_hash on document writes (tamper detection, DI-B2512CB3), services/ui review highlight renderer (DI-E81545BE), libs/ner/context_engine.py assertion evidence windows (DI-23822663), CodingReview correction event schema + services/api correction endpoints (DI-4F67189B), services/api/app/routers/audit.py + services/fhir_api/app/routers/audit_event.py audit trail APIs (DI-09E26C1D). Code-gap (tracked in improvements-backlog): append-only write-once enforcement + 7-year retention policy engine for DI-080A2454 - current retention is infra-level not application-enforced.

nodes.title: CRUD Knowledge tabs (Context Rules, Surface Forms, Domains, Terminology)
nodes.description: Four Next.js pages under services/ui/src/app/settings/ that together form the CRUD half of the Knowledge area. Each page now uses the @leo/design-system chrome primitives (StatHero + ToolbarActions, plus SegmentedTabs or FilterBar where the interaction calls for it) and a body primitive matched to the data shape:    - Context Rules: ReviewListCard rows with ProgressiveReveal     for the plain-English description and worked example,     SegmentedTabs to filter by source (verifier / surface form /     ConText / dictionary), Export PDF and Add rule via     ToolbarActions.   - Surface Forms: existing concept-group cards retained for     alias-chip + AI-suggestion editing, restyled to the     design-system tokens, wrapped in StatHero + FilterBar +     ToolbarActions chrome (Audit duplicates, Add SNOMED concept).   - Domains: motion-enabled DomainCard grid (data-testid:     domains-grid) using framer-motion for hover and tap     feedback, SegmentedTabs to filter by source, Create area     ToolbarAction gated on platform_admin via showCreateButton.   - Terminology: tone-accented PackageCard list (one per     terminology package) plus a streaming LogPanel     (data-testid: terminology-log-panel), StatHero with the     live Neo4j knowledge-graph counts, Refresh ToolbarAction.  All pre-existing data-loading, write and streaming handlers stay wired so there is zero behaviour change beyond the chrome and body redesign.

nodes.title: Three-Tier Decision Engine Module
nodes.description: Deterministic decision matrix that classifies each extracted entity into Tier 1 (auto-code), Tier 2 (code with audit flag / review), or Tier 3 (do not code / review) based on assertion, context detection status, terminology confidence, surface form approval, and disorder verdict. Mode-aware routing maps tiers to different actions in HITL vs autonomous mode. Pure function with no side effects.

nodes.title: Tier classifier v2 (libs/coding_engine/tier_classifier.py + post_processing integration)
nodes.description: Tier classifier enhanced with _TierThresholds dataclass and per-semantic-tag _TIER_THRESHOLDS map, effective_score = min(terminology_score, extractor_confidence), TIER1_EXTRACTOR_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR=0.80, and new demotion rules for assertion_parity_failed and disorder_verdict='gate_failed'. Post-processing stack in libs/pipeline/post_processing.py snapshots the LLM-assigned assertion and applies the parity check after all deterministic layers. Tier-classify subgraph in libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/tier_classify.py passes the new fields to classify_tier().

nodes.title: Coding Verification Consensus Function
nodes.description: Verifies terminology index matches using dual-model consensus, returning correct, incorrect, or uncertain. Mode-aware fail behaviour: autonomous defaults to uncertain (do not auto-approve), HITL defaults to correct (let human review). Reuses the generic consensus runner (DO-LEO-AI-023) with a domain-specific system prompt and verdict parser.

nodes.title: Terminology index match verifier with mode-aware fail behaviour
nodes.description: The system SHALL verify terminology index matches using dual-model consensus, returning correct, incorrect, or uncertain -- with mode-aware fail behaviour: autonomous mode defaults to uncertain (do not auto-code unverified matches), HITL mode defaults to correct (let human review)

nodes.title: Editable rule review dialog with versioned write-back
nodes.description: Two-column centred MUI Dialog (~1100 px) for editing pending AppropriatenessRule logic before approval. Reviewers can replace, add, or remove SNOMED concepts, change AT_LEAST minimums, edit demographic checks, and switch group kinds (AND / OR / NOT / AT_LEAST). The right column hosts a debounced /api/terminology/search panel bound to the focused chip or "Add concept" target.  Saving sends action="edit" with an updates payload to the existing decision endpoint. The new apply_rule_edit service validates the tree (depth, node count, structural rules, SNOMED concept existence), writes a brand-new :AppropriatenessRule node with status='active', links it to the same Recommendation, supersedes the predecessor via [:SUPERSEDES], and writes an immutable GuidanceAuditEvent.  Removed surfaces (per DI-LEO-AI-154): duplicated NICE recommendation block inside the edit surface (replaced with collapsible "View NICE source" link), and the redundant plain-English summary in the session-approved card (the recommendation_text is now shown directly).

nodes.title: Production Coding Worker WorkflowEngine Routing
nodes.description: Implements production cutover from CodingPipeline to WorkflowEngine for coding jobs. Adds encounter_loader subgraph to hydrate encounter text from Neo4j during runtime, removes encounter text from queue payloads, and keeps SSE progress compatibility through Redis pub/sub events.

nodes.title: Production coding worker uses WorkflowEngine + encounter_loader subgraph
nodes.description: The production coding worker SHALL execute coding jobs through the WorkflowEngine using PlanDefinition pd-gp-encounter-coding for all coding modes (extract_encounter, extract_patient, and all). Encounter narrative text SHALL NOT be transported in queue message payloads and SHALL instead be loaded at runtime from Neo4j by a dedicated encounter_loader subgraph step before extraction.

nodes.title: Training Data tab chrome composed from @leo/design-system
nodes.description: Rewrites the top section of GoldDatasetPanel.tsx -- header + toolbar actions, stats grid, progress banner, and primary segmented tab control -- to consume the shared primitives StatHero, MetricTile, ProgressStrip, SegmentedTabs, and ToolbarActions. All existing state (tab, candidateStats, goldStats, syntheticStats, exportLoading) and all existing handlers (handleTabChange, handleExport, handleDedupePreview, setDedupeDialogOpen) are preserved; only the rendering layer is swapped.

nodes.title: Training Data tab chrome migrates to design-system primitives
nodes.description: The Training Data tab (the body of /admin/knowledge?tab=training-data, implemented in services/ui/src/components/gold-dataset/GoldDatasetPanel.tsx) SHALL render its upper chrome -- header, stat tiles, progress strip, segmented tabs, and toolbar actions -- through the shared @leo/design-system primitives shipped in DI-LEO-AI-142 (StatHero/MetricTile, ProgressStrip, SegmentedTabs, ToolbarActions). The existing candidate list body, gold label review body, synthetic generation body, and all dialogs MUST continue to function without behavioural regression.

nodes.title: Knowledge hub: merged admin Clinical + Knowledge pages
nodes.description: Consolidates the admin "Clinical Setup" page and the admin "Knowledge" page into a single 8-tab page at /admin/knowledge. Deletes /admin/clinical and adds permanent redirects from every legacy URL (/admin/clinical, /admin/clinical?tab=<k>, /admin/pathways, /admin/domains, /admin/terminology) to the matching /admin/knowledge?tab=<k>. Updates AppShell ADMIN_NAV_ITEMS to remove the Clinical nav item and fold its route coverage into the Knowledge activePrefix. Extends the admin-url-audit Jest test with '/admin/clinical' so re-introductions fail CI.

nodes.title: Multi-label NER - spancat component, layer 5 nesting refinement, prompt preservation
nodes.description: Eight coordinated changes to support multi-label span classification:  1. base.cfg: pipeline switched from ["transformer","ner"] to    ["transformer","spancat"]. NER component block replaced with    SpanCategorizer.v1 using ngram_range_suggester (min_size=1,    max_size=10) and TransformerListener. Score weights updated to    spans_sc_f. Suggester upgraded from ngram_suggester sizes=[1..5]    to ngram_range_suggester max_size=10 to cover entity spans up to    10 tokens (p95 of gold-label corpus), recovering 11.6% of training    spans that were silently dropped by the 5-token cap.  2. label_exporter._record_to_spacy_doc(): seen_tokens dedup guard    removed. doc.ents assignment replaced with doc.spans["sc"] so    overlapping and co-located spans are all written to DocBin.  3. evaluator._build_per_label(): reads spans_sc_per_type instead    of ents_per_type. Score threshold checks updated to spans_sc_f.  4. model_inference /extract: iterates doc.spans.get("sc", []) for    post-spancat models; falls back to doc.ents with a logged warning    for pre-spancat model artifacts (backward compatibility).  5. post_processing.normalise_entity_types(): same-label nesting    suppression now only fires when both spans share an identical    normalized lookup term. Spans with the same label but different    normalized terms are both preserved.  6. extraction_v1.py: SEMANTIC TAG RULES section updated to clarify    "one semantic_tag per output entry; do not emit multiple entries    for the same

nodes.title: Auth, role-state and tenant-scope middleware
nodes.description:
Design output documenting the authN/authZ surface: `libs/auth/role_state.py` (RoleState, canonical role set, selected-role workflow), `libs/auth/tenant_context.py` (tenant scope), `libs/auth/practitioner_org_context.py` (clinician-org binding), `libs/auth/service_auth.py`, `libs/auth/org_scope.py`, and `services/api/app/routers/auth.py`. Azure Key Vault-backed secrets (`libs/keyvault/loader.py`, `libs/azure/credentials.py`).

Gaps (batch-15 Theme B/C): formalised token lifecycle documentation (UN-A031A603), explicit conflict-of-interest attestation artefact per review (UN-17724530), and physical database-level tenant separation (UN-412D1ECD currently implemented as logical tenant-scoped Cypher rather than per-tenant DB). Backlogged.

nodes.title: Coding Review UI
nodes.description: Provides the user interface for reviewing AI-generated clinical coding suggestions. Displays encounter narrative with highlighted entity spans, candidate SNOMED codes with plain-language confidence bands (low/medium/high), and controls for accepting, rejecting, or modifying each suggestion. Supports side-by-side view of source text and coded entities.

nodes.title: Assertion-aware analytics queries for CCI and cohort filters
nodes.description: Adds a _CONFIRMED_ASSERTIONS constant (frozenset{"present","historical"}) to both cci.py and cohorts.py. Every Cypher query that traverses a [:DOCUMENTS] relationship now aliases it as [r:DOCUMENTS] and includes:    AND coalesce(r.assertion, 'present') IN $assertions  (CCI)   AND coalesce(r.assertion, 'present') IN $confirmed_assertions  (cohorts)  The coalesce guard preserves backwards compatibility: encounters created before assertion tracking was introduced carry no assertion property and are treated as 'present'.  'historical' is included in confirmed assertions because CCI is a lifetime comorbidity index (e.g. a previous stroke still counts). Cohort filtering also includes 'historical' so ex-smoker SNOMED codes correctly match the ever_smoker filter.

nodes.title: Analytics filters exclude non-confirmed assertions from CCI and cohort filters
nodes.description: The system SHALL exclude coded clinical entities with a non-confirmed assertion (i.e. assertions other than present or historical) from all analytics computations, including Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) scoring and cohort condition/smoking-status filters. A coalesce guard SHALL treat a missing assertion as present.

nodes.title: PageIntro + HelpPopover + CoachMark + ProgressiveReveal + GlossaryTerm + glossary.ts + readability.ts
nodes.description: Five explanation primitives exported from services/ui/src/components/ui/. A glossary module in services/ui/src/lib/glossary.ts provides (label, clinicalTerm, plainLanguage) triplets keyed by termId. A readability utility computes Flesch-Kincaid Grade to gate shipped copy in CI. - PageIntro: SSR-safe, persists collapse state per   screen in localStorage. - HelpPopover: MUI Popover with role='dialog',   aria-labelledby, Escape-closes. - CoachMark: portal-rendered overlay tied to an anchor   ref; respects prefers-reduced-motion; dismissal   persists in localStorage 'leo-tour-<tour-id>-done'. - ProgressiveReveal: MUI Collapse wrapped with   aria-expanded disclosure button. - GlossaryTerm: renders an underlined span that opens a   HelpPopover with plainLanguage; tree-shakeable import.

nodes.title: Five reusable explanation primitives (PageIntro, HelpPopover, CoachMark, ProgressiveReveal, GlossaryTerm)
nodes.description: The LEO UI SHALL expose five reusable explanation primitives (PageIntro, HelpPopover, CoachMark, ProgressiveReveal, GlossaryTerm) that every screen consumes to answer, for the current persona, (a) Why am I here, (b) How do I do the task, (c) What will happen next. GlossaryTerm MUST read its definition from a single source-of-truth glossary keyed by clinical term. All patient-reachable copy rendered through these primitives MUST be written at Flesch-Kincaid Grade level 9 or below.

nodes.title: Training pipeline quality - span realign, assertion filter, golden set, warm-start, active learning
nodes.description: Six quality capabilities added to the training pipeline: 1. Span realignment: _realign_entity() uses find_span() to re-derive    character offsets from surface text before DocBin creation. 2. Assertion filter: entities with assertion in TRAINING_EXCLUDE_ASSERTIONS    (default: negated, hypothetical, family_history, possible) are removed. 3. Per-label F1: job.to_dict() adds per_label_f1 top-level shortcut. 4. Warm-start: TRAINING_BASE_MODEL_VERSION triggers download and NER    weight initialisation from promoted blob. 5. Golden evaluation set: GoldLabel.frozen_golden_set flag, golden_set_queries.py,    second evaluation pass in evaluator.py, MODEL_MIN_GOLDEN_F1 gate. 6. Active learning: POST /candidates/score scores by token entropy,    GET /candidates/active-learning-queue returns sorted queue.

nodes.title: Shared libs/metrics module for NCDA interval KPIs
nodes.description: Extracts the NCDA interval KPI math (days_presentation_to_referral, days_referral_to_diagnosis, days_diagnosis_to_treatment) into a pure-math module at libs/metrics/ with zero Neo4j or LLM dependencies. The runtime kpi_calculator and the one-shot scripts/build_ncda_export.py both import days_between, pick_earliest_milestone, and compute_interval_kpis from this module so they produce identical numbers. The Neo4j I/O (milestone fetch, consultations-before-referral count, persistence) remains in the analyzer.

nodes.title: Dual Neo4j Database Architecture
nodes.description: Implements two physically separate Neo4j database instances: one for patient and clinical data, one for terminology and reference data. This separation ensures that a breach or misconfiguration in the terminology layer cannot expose patient-identifiable information, and allows independent scaling, backup, and access-control policies for each data domain.

nodes.title: Extraction quality LLM check before terminology
nodes.description: Adds a relation-linking stage and a single-turn extraction quality check before terminology resolution. The quality check can drop noisy entities, correct assertion and semantic tag fields, add missed clinically explicit mentions, and correct/add relation links for body-site and qualifier context. The check uses a constrained JSON contract and attaches provenance markers for retraining. Referral procedure phrases are protected from uncertain assertion downgrades by a deterministic guard. Conditional routing sends changed extraction payloads to HITL queue.

nodes.title: Analytics Dashboard Service
nodes.description: An API layer that serves aggregated metrics, key performance indicators, deprivation-index breakdowns, benchmark comparisons, and cohort summaries to the front-end dashboard. Each router handles a specific analytics domain and queries the patient Neo4j instance for real-time or cached results.

nodes.title: SpanResolver utility (libs/ner/span_resolver.py)
nodes.description: New shared utility class SpanResolver that resolves absolute character (start, end) offsets for LLM-extracted terms within an encounter. Uses sentence-level and encounter-wide cursors to disambiguate repeated mentions. Consumed by both services/coding_worker/app/pipeline/llm_extractor.py and libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/_extractor.py so both LLM extractor code paths produce accurate spans.

nodes.title: Domain-Driven Episode Detector
nodes.description: Replaces hardcoded SNOMED frozensets in the episode detector with live configuration loaded from AuditDomain/ValueSet nodes in Neo4j. Key changes: - AuditDomain gains episodeDetector boolean (domains.py + UI) - ValueSet gains assertionFilter string list (domains.py, registry.py, UI) - NCDADomain dataclass gains assertion_filter field (registry.py) - _ANCHOR_QUERY returns r.assertion per DOCUMENTS relationship - _classify_anchor_rows() applies concept_id + assertion double-filter - DomainRegistry bootstrap raises instead of from_defaults() fallback - EpisodeOfCare nodes carry domain_id property

nodes.title: Safety-net detector, persistence and pipeline subgraph
nodes.description:
Design output documenting the safety-netting surface: `services/analysis_worker/app/analyzers/safety_net_detector.py`, `safety_net_persistence.py`, pipeline subgraph `libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/safety_net.py`, reference-range seeding in `scripts/seed_reference_ranges.py`, and near-miss cleanup in `scripts/delete_near_miss_alerts.py`.

Gaps (batch-13 theme C): three-band severity classification is implemented but configurable follow-up window worklist, auto-suppression on confirmed clinical response, and immutable clinician-id action recording are partial; see improvements-backlog.

nodes.title: LLM Prompt Safety Utilities Module
nodes.description: Centralised module providing three prompt safety utilities used at all LLM call sites across the LEO AI pipeline:  INJECTION_GUARD (str): System prompt prefix that instructs the LLM to treat all content in data blocks as inert, regardless of its appearance. Prevents the model from following embedded instruction-like text.  sanitise_for_prompt(text, max_chars=16000): Applies a compiled regex (_INJECTION_RE) covering 15+ injection pattern families to replace matching text with [FILTERED]. Logs the substitution count at WARNING level. Truncates the result to max_chars. Default limit of 16000 chars (~4 A4 pages) preserves full clinical context to prevent coding errors from silent truncation.  cap_llm_response(raw, max_chars=1000): Truncates raw LLM output to max_chars before any parse function can operate on it. Logs a WARNING containing "response-stuffing" when truncation occurs.

nodes.title: UI Safety, Accessibility, and Usability Remediation
nodes.description: Comprehensive remediation of 48 findings from the IEC 62366-1 / WCAG 2.2 usability engineering audit (DC-UE-001). Covers 5 phases: Phase 1: Safety-critical confirmation dialogs and error handling Phase 2: WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility remediation Phase 3: Major usability and remaining safety fixes Phase 4: Comprehensive accessibility label remediation Phase 5: Minor issues and information architecture Plus a preventive .cursor rule for future development.

nodes.title: Three-Stream SurfaceFormTask Creation with Two-Reviewer Gate
nodes.description: Implements three input streams feeding SurfaceFormTask nodes. Stream A reads audit gaps. Stream B defers MAPS_TO creation from resolve_coding_review to a SurfaceFormTask pending second approval. Stream C creates tasks from LLM high-confidence terms, capped at 20/day with auto-pause at queue depth 50. Source badge displayed in ReviewCard.

nodes.title: Relation reviewer UI with policy-aware triplets
nodes.description:
Design output documenting the gold-dataset relation reviewer UI that renders source -> type -> target triplets with a LinkOff warning when no relation is set. Surfaces accept/reject/undo from a single card.

Gap (DI-3035F221 partial): per-pair SNOMED structural policy explanation is not rendered inline on the reviewer card; extraction_method chip not yet shown. Tracked in improvements-backlog batch-05.

nodes.title: Per-semantic-tag tier thresholds, extractor confidence fusion, and assertion parity gating
nodes.description: Updates to the three-tier decision engine and post-processing stack:  - classify_tier accepts semantic_tag, extractor_confidence, and   assertion_parity_failed and uses a per-tag thresholds table   (disorder 0.92, finding/situation 0.93, procedure 0.94,   substance/product/observable 0.96-0.97; default 0.95). - effective_score = min(terminology_score, extractor_confidence)   with a hard floor (0.80) below which tier-1 is blocked with reason   ``low_extractor_confidence``. - A new assertion_parity snapshot in post_processing records the   LLM's original assertion before the deterministic layers run, and   compares it against the final assertion after the stack   completes. Disagreements set ``assertion_parity_failed=True``,   which caps the tier gate at tier 2 with reason ``assertion_parity``. - tier_classify subgraph passes all three new arguments through to   classify_tier.

nodes.title: Smart Few-Shot Selection + Prompt Caching
nodes.description: Runtime prompt assembly enhancement with static core examples, dynamic few-shot retrieval by similarity, and Bedrock cache-point marking. Includes PromptConfig schema/API/UI support for maxFewShot and core flags persisted in Neo4j.

nodes.title: PromptConfig with smart few-shot selection and prompt caching
nodes.description: The system SHALL provide PromptConfig controls for smart few-shot selection and prompt caching, including a configurable maximum few-shot count, a per-example core flag, and provider-aware runtime selection of relevant examples while preserving de-identification and auditability.

nodes.title: Disorder verifier fail-closed with explicit GATE_FAILED verdict
nodes.description: - DisorderVerdict enum gains ``GATE_FAILED = "gate_failed"``. - ``_fail_verdict_for_mode`` returns ``gate_failed`` in both HITL   and autonomous modes (and any unknown mode). - ``verify_disorder`` writes ``disorder_verdict`` on the entity   dict for downstream layers and, on GATE_FAILED, sets   ``__needs_review__=True`` and ``__gate_failed__=True``. - The post-processing disorder-gate layer recognises GATE_FAILED   and routes the entity to review rather than auto-suppress or   auto-code.

nodes.title: SafetyNetAlert with Dedup, Escalation, and LoopConfig Kill Switch
nodes.description: Implements SafetyNetAlert creation with deduplication (minimum 100 encounters, new critical terms only or >3% drop), time-based escalation (48h/7d/14d), auto-pause at 14d, LoopConfig Neo4j node as kill switch, audit quality API router, and UI notification badge.

nodes.title: NER + SNOMED coding surface with assertion handling
nodes.description: Umbrella DO for UN-0374FE26 SNOMED coding core. Components: libs/ner NER pipeline (DI-1795254D, DI-4247C7E5), libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs SNOMED linker and assertion layer (DI-31126C6C, DI-375C7EB1), libs/pipeline/post_processing.py 9-layer post-processing, services/coding_worker runtime pipeline. Code-gap flagged in improvements-backlog: gold F1 evaluator for DI-12015DBC and per-semantic-tag threshold drift monitoring for DI-88C8BBCD.

nodes.title: Gold-label review dialog: chrome sub-components
nodes.description: Five focused React components that replace the inline chrome of the legacy GoldLabelDetailDialog inside GoldDatasetPanel.tsx. Each component is a pure presentation shell that receives all state and handlers from the parent. The parent (still inline in GoldDatasetPanel.tsx for now) owns business logic so we can swap chrome without risking the SVG arc renderer, surface form mapping, subdomain popover, or relation suggestion pipeline.  Sub-components:   - DialogTitleStrip: status pill (uncoded + suggested     counts), copy / guidelines / shortcuts / close cluster.   - SuggestionsPanel: collapsible "Recommended links" list     with single Accept-all action.   - DeleteConfirmPanel: slide-in destructive confirmation     with suppress-from-pipeline checkbox.   - DialogActionsBar: single primary action whose label     morphs based on suggestion state, Skip-to-next as     tertiary, Delete behind a kebab.   - AddTermPopover: extracted target for the future     "Add a missing term" popover (currently unused by the     parent panel; lands in Phase 2b with the deeper body     decomposition).

nodes.title: NER-first extraction routing and deterministic pre-filtering
nodes.description: Implements deterministic filtering of non-evidence sentence lines and routes extraction to the model inference backend when extraction_method is set to ner. The model provider calls the /extract endpoint on the model inference service and maps responses into canonical ExtractionItem records.

nodes.title: Single-source GoldLabel training data and simplified operations workflow
nodes.description: Consolidates model-training data flow onto Knowledge Graph GoldLabel. - Adds a migration utility from legacy TrainingLabel to GoldLabel. - Updates training worker export to read completed GoldLabel records. - Simplifies operations workspace to focus on gold-data metrics and model   training actions, with direct routing to /admin/gold-dataset for data   correction workflows.

nodes.title: Knowledge Graph GoldLabel as single source of truth for training data
nodes.description: The system SHALL treat Knowledge Graph GoldLabel data as the single source of truth for model training by (a) migrating eligible legacy TrainingLabel records into GDPR-isolated TrainingCandidate and GoldLabel nodes, (b) exporting training DocBin files directly from completed GoldLabel records in the Knowledge Graph, and (c) aligning operations training UX to reference gold-dataset data and workflows instead of legacy TrainingLabel lifecycle states.

nodes.title: Episode builder subgraph with classification + DQ
nodes.description:
Design output documenting the episode construction + classification surface: `libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/episode.py`, prompts in `libs/prompts/episode_builder_v1.py` and `episode_builder_output_schema.py`, DQ checks in `libs/dq/episodes.py`, tests in `tests/test_episode_builder.py`.

Gaps (batch-14 theme A): BD696225 human-review gate before audit reporting; 736B698B 85% F1 accuracy gate; A0579B64 reporting block on unresolved flags; deterministic construction invariant (FF9C74E2).

nodes.title: Audit Event System
nodes.description: Provides a structured audit event emitter and FHIR-compatible audit event endpoint. Every auditable action in the system -- user logins, data access, configuration changes, model invocations -- is captured, timestamped, and persisted so the organisation can demonstrate compliance during regulatory inspections.

nodes.title: Centralised area intro copy + KnowledgePageLayout rollout + feature flag default
nodes.description: Implements DI-LEO-AI-139. Adds services/ui/src/lib/areaCopy.ts with role-aware intro copy for all 9 major areas, wraps every target landing page in KnowledgePageLayout, and flips the NEXT_PUBLIC_ROLE_FIRST default in next.config.mjs so the role-first shell ships to all users.

nodes.title: Test patient data model, copy-from-real-patient service, and aspect-aware library API
nodes.description:
Back-end work that lets test patients be stored in the same shape as real patients and copied from a real record.

Source files (created or rebuilt during Phase A):
- libs/cypher/test_patient_queries.py (rebuilt around :TestPatient label, is_test flag and aspect tag)
- services/api/app/services/test_patient_clone.py (new -- copies a real :Patient to :TestPatient, removes identifying details, adds test_ prefix)
- services/api/app/services/test_patient_service.py (extended for the four aspects: nlp, episodes, guidelines, summarisation)
- services/api/app/routers/test_patients.py (extended with aspect query parameter and clone endpoint)

Implements DI-59824215 (test patient data model). Verified by VT-A.

nodes.title: Disorder verifier v2 with fail-closed GATE_FAILED verdict (libs/llm_client/disorder_verifier.py)
nodes.description: DisorderVerdict enum extended with GATE_FAILED member. _fail_verdict_for_mode() simplified to return GATE_FAILED for all modes (HITL, autonomous, unknown). verify_disorder() records disorder_verdict on the entity, and on GATE_FAILED sets __needs_review__=True and __gate_failed__=True to prevent silent auto-coding. Post-processing stack handles GATE_FAILED explicitly in _apply_disorder_gate.

nodes.title: Overcoded CodingReview Creation with Urgent Queue and 48h SLA Alert
nodes.description: Audit Phase 3 identifies overcoded items. Each overcoded item creates a CodingReview node with review_type='overcoded' and priority='urgent'. These appear in a dedicated urgent section in the ReviewSection UI above the general queue. A background check creates a SafetyNetAlert if any urgent item remains unreviewed after 48 hours.

nodes.title: Spinal-TNM scope guard and LLM prompt disambiguation rule
nodes.description: Two coordinated changes that form a dual-layer defence against spinal vertebral notation being misclassified as cancer TNM staging:  Layer 1 -- LLM prompt (extraction_v1.py):   A new negative extraction rule in the DO NOT EXTRACT section instructs   the extraction model not to label isolated vertebral level tokens (C1-C7,   T1-T12, L1-L5, S1-S5) as staging scale or observable entity when the   sentence contains spinal anatomical or physiotherapy context signals.  Layer 2 -- Post-processing scope guard (scope_guard.py):   A new is_spinal_context() predicate and a matching check block inside   reclassify_assertion(). When a standalone TNM component token (T0-T4,   N0-N3, M0-M1 with optional c/p/y/r prefix) appears in a sentence with   spinal markers and no full TNM triplet, reclassify_assertion() returns   SUPPRESSED. The _apply_scope_guard_to_dicts() caller in post_processing.py   removes the entity before terminology resolution.

nodes.title: Bitmap Store, Guideline Compiler, and Evaluator in Terminology API
nodes.description: Four-file implementation in terminology_api: BitmapStore wraps pyroaring BitMap with Redis persistence and deterministic BLAKE2b key scheme; GuidelineCompiler reads active AppropriatenessRules from Neo4j and compiles them into versioned Roaring bitmaps; GuidelineEvaluator performs microsecond reqAll/forbid intersection checks against patient SNOMED codes; FastAPI router exposes evaluation, compile, versions, activate, and status endpoints.

nodes.title: Surface forms CRUD with duplicate audit and match frequency
nodes.description:
Design output documenting the Settings > Surface Forms management surface across API (`services/terminology_api/app/routers/surface_forms.py`), Cypher (`services/terminology_api/app/queries/terminology.py` AUDIT_SURFACE_FORM_DUPLICATES, DEDUPLICATE_SURFACE_FORM_RELS, LIST/GROUPED/UPSERT/DELETE_SURFACE_FORM*), and the UI page at `services/ui/src/app/settings/surface-forms/page.tsx`.

Covers DI-30D95132 (CRUD + duplicate rejection + match frequency via grouped list). Duplicate audit queries expose mappings that conflict on (text, concept_id) and support dedup/merge operations.

Gap (DI-9FD54AD6, tracked in improvements-backlog batch-08): no staging -> approval -> versioned-rollout workflow; writes go directly to active KG.

nodes.title: createLeoTheme() factory in @leo/design-system consumed by services/ui ThemeRegistry
nodes.description: The MUI theme moves out of services/ui into the shared design-system workspace package. A single exported factory, createLeoTheme, reads tokens from services/design-system/src/ tokens/color, /spacing, and /typography and returns a complete MUI Theme. services/ui/src/components/ThemeRegistry.tsx imports the factory from "@leo/design-system/theme" and instantiates it once; the old services/ui/src/theme.ts file is removed. The design-system package.json exposes the new path via its exports map so consumers can import it without reaching into src/. Static-analysis tests are updated to read the new location.

nodes.title: Centralised MUI theme factory (createLeoTheme) sourced from design-system tokens
nodes.description: The MUI theme used by services/ui SHALL be produced by a factory function (createLeoTheme) exported from @leo/design-system/theme, not by a theme object defined inside services/ui. The factory SHALL consume its palette, typography, and shape values from the design-system tokens in services/design-system/src/tokens/* so that a single change to a token propagates to every MUI component and every role-first surface.

nodes.title: Specialist outcome letter anchors and inferred benign episode closure
nodes.description: Extends anchor detection with specialist_outcome_letter_anchors from SNOMED coded DOCUMENTS rows (ValueSet-backed) and from document_transfer encounter metadata plus text sentinels. Extends episode build for open referral-only episodes to mark completed with HITL when a qualifying letter and absence of post-letter treatment anchors align with temporal rules after the post-specialist stale threshold.

nodes.title: Specialist outcome letter inference for benign episode closure
nodes.description: The episode detection system SHALL classify specialist correspondence (clinic letters, record artifacts in the configured audit subdomain, and document_transfer encounters with classification_encounter_purpose containing clinic_letter) into a specialist_outcome_letter milestone bucket. For referral-only open episodes where specialist_seen is true, a specialist visit date is stored, at least one specialist_outcome_letter anchor falls on or after the specialist visit date and within 60 days after it, on or after the referral date, no treatment_start anchor occurs between the letter date and 120 days after the letter date inclusive, and calendar days since the specialist visit exceed the stale_post_specialist threshold (90 days), the system SHALL persist the episode as status completed with hitl_flag true and an explicit hitl_reason describing inferred benign completion. Otherwise existing diagnosis-led and stale-close behaviour is unchanged.

nodes.title: LEO presents each user the slimmest viable experience for their role
nodes.description: LEO serves four very different working lives from the same app: a clinician opening a patient record between appointments, a coding or audit staff member working a queue of tasks, a QA/RA lead investigating the product own behaviour, and a platform admin looking after tenants and users. Today the nav shows the same long list to everyone. Junior staff and older clinicians in particular tell us the app feels like it is for someone else and that the extra choice slows them down. The user need: on first sign-in the user picks a role once. After that, the app lands them on the right home screen, shows a short nav for their role, and tucks the rest behind a single Advanced tray. A user with more than one role can switch from a clearly labelled switcher in the top right. Switching role never hides clinical data; it only changes emphasis and layout.

nodes.title: Platform must enforce physical database-level separation of patient data between tenants with automated provisioning and deprovision
nodes.description: As a platform administrator, I need the system to enforce physical separation of patient data between tenants so that a misconfiguration or access error in one tenant cannot expose patient records from another.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer needs a complete tamper-evident audit trail of all review decisions exportable for regulatory inspection and post-market surveillance
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer, I need a complete, exportable audit trail of all review decisions, so that Mizaic can produce evidence of clinical oversight for regulatory inspection, customer due diligence, and post-market surveillance without manual reconstruction.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a coding correction needs full dependency mapping and terminology validation before approving a code change
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a proposed coding correction, I need to verify that the corrected code accurately maps to the intended clinical concept, so that downstream analytics, pathway logic, and reporting are not corrupted by an incorrect or ambiguous code assignment.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a guideline update needs to verify source accuracy and implementation safety as independently evidenced decisions
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a proposed guideline update, I need to verify that the update accurately reflects the source guideline and that the implementation is clinically safe, so that the device continues to support evidence-based care after the update is applied.

nodes.title: System protects patient data with encryption, authentication, and authorisation controls
nodes.description: Data protection officers need the system to protect patient data with encryption at rest and in transit, strong authentication via Azure AD / Entra ID, granular authorisation controls, and compliance with NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT) requirements. The system must support data residency within UK geography, implement least-privilege access, and provide security monitoring and incident response capabilities.

nodes.title: Consensus arbitrator third-verdict warning for anomaly detection
nodes.description: The dual-model consensus runner (libs/llm_client/consensus.py) SHALL emit a WARNING-level log message with the keyword 'consensus.arbitrator_third_verdict' whenever the Sonnet arbitrator returns a verdict that differs from both the AWS and Azure primary model verdicts. The warning MUST include the arbitrator verdict, the AWS verdict, and the Azure verdict. This warning is an audit control signal: an unexpected third verdict from the arbitrator may indicate that an LLM model has been jailbroken, subjected to prompt injection, or is producing anomalous output.

nodes.title: Per-episode specialist visit attribution without cross-pathway contamination
nodes.description: Clinical quality managers and auditors need each cancer investigation episode to carry only the specialist visit that genuinely belongs to it. When a patient has multiple cancer referral episodes sharing the same cancer site (e.g. two breast 2WW referrals in different years), a specialist clinic visit from the first pathway must not be attributed to the second. Incorrect attribution produces false stale_post_specialist episode counts, inflated specialist-seen rates, and inaccurate NCDA audit metrics.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need a canary rollout mechanism for new NER model versions with automatic halt on regression
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer, I need a controlled canary rollout mechanism for new NER model versions, so that regressions are detected against live traffic before a model version is fully promoted and the previous version can be automatically reinstated on failure.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need ontology-grounded relation linking to connect extracted findings to body sites, disorders, and procedures
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer developing clinical entity extraction, I need ontology-grounded relation linking so that extracted findings can be safely connected to their body sites, qualifiers, disorders, and procedures in a way that is validated against SNOMED structural rules, so that downstream pathway logic can reason about complete clinical statements rather than isolated coded entities.

nodes.title: Platform administrators need AI spend tracking and configurable pricing per tenant
nodes.description: As a platform administrator or commercial lead, I need to track AI model spend per tenant, configure a gross margin target, apply time-limited or perpetual discounts per organisation, and see platform operating costs separately from billable tenant spend — all from an admin interface without a code deployment — so that commercial operations can be managed without engineering involvement.

nodes.title: Engineering leads need the platform to follow Mizaic standard architecture and engineering design principles consistently across all services
nodes.description: As an engineering lead responsible for the LEO Core AI platform, I need all services to follow Mizaic's standard architecture and engineering design principles consistently — workflow-as-data, configuration-as-data, async fire-and-track, AI models as graph nodes, secrets from Key Vault, and enforced code quality limits — so that any engineer can onboard to any part of the codebase with predictable patterns, and the system remains maintainable and auditable as it grows.

nodes.title: Developer validating an integration needs a sandbox environment with synthetic clinical data, fault injection, and full production parity
nodes.description: As a developer validating a LEO Core AI integration, I need a sandbox environment that faithfully represents production behaviour with synthetic clinical data, so I can test against realistic scenarios including edge cases and failure conditions without risk to patient data or live systems.

nodes.title: Clinician discussing treatment options needs guideline recommendations and real-world outcome context to support informed shared decision-making
nodes.description: As a clinician discussing treatment options with a patient, I need to know what the guideline recommends and how patients with a similar profile responded to each option in practice, because supporting an informed shared decision-making conversation currently requires manually locating guideline references and outcome data from multiple sources under time pressure.

nodes.title: Audit teams need interpretable benchmark comparison charts in audit report outputs
nodes.description: As a clinical audit team member or programme manager reviewing audit report outputs, I need clear interpretable charts that compare my patient population's performance against national benchmarks, so that I can quickly identify where local performance diverges from the national picture without needing to interpret raw data tables.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author withdrawing a superseded guideline needs full dependency enumeration and mandatory resolution before deprecation can proceed
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author withdrawing a superseded guideline, I need to ensure that all dependent pathway logic, decision support rules, and user-facing content are identified and resolved before the guideline is removed, because no part of the system should continue to reference a withdrawn clinical standard after deprecation.

nodes.title: Clinical content managers need a maintainable reference range library covering normal, borderline, and critical thresholds per investigation type
nodes.description: As a clinical content manager, I need a maintainable reference range library covering normal, borderline, and critical thresholds per investigation type, so that safety netting rules are grounded in validated clinical evidence and can be kept current as guidelines change.

nodes.title: Clinical reviewers and auditors need every AI-extracted entity linked to its source text phrase with immutable provenance
nodes.description: As a clinical reviewer, clinical coder, or auditor working with AI-extracted clinical codes, I need every extracted entity to link back to the exact phrase in the source text that generated it, with the extraction method, confidence score, and assertion context visible alongside it, so that I can verify each extraction in seconds without reading the full source document, and so that a complete evidence chain exists for every coded finding.

nodes.title: Developer beginning integration needs a complete, versioned API specification available before writing any code
nodes.description: As a developer beginning integration with LEO Core AI, I need a complete, accurate, and versioned API specification available before writing any code, so I can assess integration effort and design my product architecture correctly from the start.

nodes.title: A QA lead, knowledge author or NLP reviewer needs one place to keep test patients that check every part of the AI: reading notes, building the patient story, checking guideline rules, and writing the SBAR handover
nodes.description: As a QA lead, knowledge author, NLP reviewer or clinical lead, I need one library that holds test patients I can use to check every part of the AI before a change goes live. The four parts I care about are: the AI tool that reads clinical notes and pulls out clinical codes; the AI tool that builds the patient story across encounters; the rule checker that flags safety issues against guidelines; and the AI tool that writes the SBAR handover. I want the test patients to look as close to real patients as possible. Where it helps, I want to copy a real patient, remove their identifying details, and save the result as a test patient.

nodes.title: Platform administrators need a structured guided onboarding workflow to provision new healthcare organisations safely
nodes.description: As a platform administrator, I need a structured guided onboarding workflow for provisioning a new healthcare organisation so that all configuration, data connection, and access setup steps are completed in the correct order without manual coordination.

nodes.title: Infer cancer or benign pathway outcome from post-specialist encounter signals
nodes.description: Quality leads and clinicians reviewing stale_post_specialist episodes need the system to scan the 180 days of encounters following a specialist visit and determine, from textual signals alone, whether the outcome was likely cancer (requiring further action) or benign (pathway complete). Where a clear inference can be made it should be stored with a confidence score and earliest inferred date so that time-to-outcome milestones can be calculated even when no formal SNOMED diagnosis was coded. Where no inference is possible the episode must be flagged for human review.

nodes.title: Clinical audit teams need patient records automatically shortlisted for programme relevance
nodes.description: As a clinical coder or audit programme manager, I need the system to automatically retrieve and rank patient encounters from FHIR records by relevance to the configured audit programme, so that my review effort is focused on clinically relevant encounters rather than manually filtering thousands of records.

nodes.title: Lab-value guard prevents diagnostic inference from observable measurements
nodes.description: The coding pipeline SHALL NOT infer a clinical diagnosis from a lab result value. Lab measurements (e.g. eGFR, HbA1c, creatinine, sodium, haemoglobin, cholesterol, TSH, troponin, PSA, LDH, amylase, lipase, procalcitonin, NT-proBNP, CK/CPK, lactate, AFP, CA-125, CEA) SHALL be coded only as observable entities with their numeric value and unit. A disorder entity SHALL only be generated when the encounter text explicitly states a diagnosis. The lab-value guard SHALL operate on a per-entity sentence window (not the full encounter text) to avoid false suppression of legitimate diagnoses in other parts of the encounter.

nodes.title: UN-LEO-AI-096: One consistent encounter row + search experience across encounter surfaces
nodes.description: As a clinical reviewer or training-data curator, I need /care/encounters, the /care/patients side drawer, the /admin/training Candidates dry-run queue, AND the 'Apply to similar candidates' batch dialog to share one visual language and search vocabulary -- one row primitive (ReviewListCard tone strip + chip taxonomy), one HighlightedText highlight token (#fde68a amber), one match-rationale chip row, one query-expansion vocabulary (typo + synonym maps via libs/search/term_expansion + the mirrored mission-control/encounterRelevance.ts) -- so muscle memory transfers between surfaces and a query for 'lump' surfaces the same encounters/candidates everywhere it is typed.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need a de-identified labelled training corpus with a protected holdout evaluation set
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer responsible for training and evaluating clinical NER models, I need a de-identified, labelled training corpus with a protected holdout set that is never included in any training export, so that model training and evaluation are performed on clean data without patient privacy risk, and model performance against the holdout set is a reliable indicator of real-world accuracy.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer approval process must enforce credential scoping and conflict of interest controls to constitute genuine clinical governance
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer, I need the system to enforce that only appropriately credentialed reviewers can approve changes within their defined clinical scope, so that approval decisions cannot be made by individuals without the relevant clinical authority or with a conflict of interest.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author needs a consolidated currency dashboard showing verified status and next review date for every active content component as exportable post-market surveillance evidence
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author responsible for the overall currency of the clinical knowledge base, I need a consolidated view of the last verified date and next due review for every active guideline, coding dictionary, and reference dataset, because no content component should age beyond its defined review threshold without a documented decision, and consolidated evidence of oversight is required for post-market surveillance.

nodes.title: Detect specialist letters and infer benign pathway completion when appropriate
nodes.description: Quality leads auditing cancer investigation pathways need the system to recognise when a specialist clinic letter or discharge correspondence has arrived back at the practice after a 2WW referral and specialist visit, even when full letter text is not stored. When no treatment is coded in the following months, the pathway should be able to close as completed with a clear human-review flag rather than remaining indefinitely in a stale state.

nodes.title: Clinical content managers need to maintain the surface form dictionary mapping free-text expressions to SNOMED concepts
nodes.description: As a clinical content manager, I need to maintain the dictionary of textual surface forms that map free-text expressions to SNOMED concepts, so that NER extraction accuracy reflects local clinical language and improvements are auditable.

nodes.title: Technical administrators need a unified Intelligence Console showing the AI learning loop status and next best action
nodes.description: As a clinical informatician or technical administrator responsible for the AI learning loop, I need a unified Intelligence Console that shows the health and status of every stage of the model improvement cycle in one view, with contextual guidance on the next best action, so that the loop is visible, actionable, and self-guiding without requiring expert knowledge of each individual admin subsystem.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need the NER model to classify the same text span under multiple SNOMED semantic types simultaneously
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer building a clinical entity recognition model, I need the NER pipeline to support classification of the same text span under multiple SNOMED semantic types simultaneously, so that a clinical entity that is both a disorder and a finding — or both a procedure and an observable — is correctly represented without forcing a single label that loses clinical meaning.

nodes.title: Clinical reviewers need a structured queue where every AI proposal must be validated before becoming final audit data
nodes.description: As a clinical coder or human reviewer working with AI-generated audit outputs, I need a structured review queue where every AI proposal — coded encounter, episode classification, quality alert, or clinical interpretation — is presented for my validation before it becomes final audit data, so that AI errors are caught before they affect patient records, audit reporting, or downstream clinical decisions.

nodes.title: Clinical NLP pipeline must completely capture test result values for observable entities
nodes.description: The post-processing pipeline attaches numeric values (e.g. 7.2 mmol/L) to observable entities during Layer 6 value-unit linking. However, two common clinical patterns are not captured: 1) String-based results - A test result expressed as positive, negative, or borderline is reclassified as a qualifier_value entity but is never formally linked to its parent observable entity. Downstream analytics cannot query eGFR result = negative without this link. 2) Value before entity - When a numeric or string result appears before the observable name in the encounter text (e.g. 7.2 mmol/L HbA1c or negative -- Urine culture), no value is attached because the pipeline relies only on extracted measurement entities and does not scan the raw text window preceding the observable. Both gaps mean that observable entities leave the pipeline with obs.value = None even when a result is clearly present in the encounter text, degrading the quality of clinical data extracted for audit and pathway analysis.

nodes.title: Clinician reviewing investigation results needs guideline escalation thresholds and comparable result trajectories to avoid missing actionable findings
nodes.description: As a clinician reviewing investigation results, I need to know what result thresholds the guideline defines as escalation triggers and how comparable results affected pathway progression in practice, because without structured signposting actionable results can be missed or misinterpreted, leading to delayed diagnosis and patient harm.

nodes.title: Clinical auditors need related encounters automatically grouped into structured clinical episodes
nodes.description: As a clinical auditor, I need related patient encounters to be automatically grouped into structured clinical episodes linked to pathway milestones, so that end-to-end patient journeys are visible for review and reporting without manual reconstruction from individual encounter records.

nodes.title: Junior clinical and coding staff can complete audit, coding review, and pathway tasks on LEO without prior product training
nodes.description: A large share of real LEO users are new staff: medical students, F1/F2 doctors, practice nurses in their first year, trainee coders, and apprentices. Their needs are different from experienced clinicians. They are efficient if the product explains why they are here, what each thing does, and what will happen next. They are unsafe if the product assumes mastery. Existing user needs assume a clinical audit lead or coding specialist persona. There is no explicit design input anywhere requiring explanation patterns, onboarding tours, or progressive reveal. This UN creates that requirement.

nodes.title: Care Overview PageIntro and accessible summary card typography
nodes.description: The Care Overview page (services/ui/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx) SHALL render the shared PageIntro primitive as the first block below the date filter so that, on first load, a junior staff member or older clinician sees a plain-language explanation of why they are on this page, how to read the four summary cards and two chart rows, and what the date filter changes. The chart section titles and their supporting descriptions SHALL meet Flesch-Kincaid Grade level 9 or below. The four summary StatCard values SHALL remain single-number focal points with larger (>=2rem) numerals and plain-language captions; uppercase chip-style labels on summary cards SHALL be softened to sentence case with 12px minimum font size.

nodes.title: Clinician preparing a clinic list needs pathway stage context and comparable patient profiles to prioritise preparation time
nodes.description: As a clinician preparing for a clinic session, I need a per-patient summary of outstanding pathway actions, current stage against guideline timelines, and how patients with a similar profile were managed at the same point, because manual preparation across multiple systems is time-consuming and risks missing clinically important context before the appointment.

nodes.title: Developer maintaining a product built on LEO Core AI needs a predictable versioning and deprecation policy to plan upgrade work
nodes.description: As a developer maintaining a product built on LEO Core AI, I need a predictable versioning and deprecation policy, so I can plan upgrade work without being surprised by breaking changes or forced into emergency remediations.

nodes.title: Platform administrators need a data quality engine with configurable rules, per-episode results, and an exportable governance sitrep
nodes.description: As a platform administrator, I need a structured data quality assessment across all processed episodes and encounters with a consolidated sitrep exportable for governance reporting, so that data completeness and coding accuracy issues are detected before they corrupt audit outputs.

nodes.title: Clinical coders need free-text encounter narratives automatically coded to SNOMED CT
nodes.description: As a clinical coder reviewing AI outputs, I need free-text clinical narratives to be automatically coded to SNOMED CT with confidence scores, negation detection, and assertion context — present, historical, family history, suspected — so that manual coding time is reduced and AI proposals can be efficiently verified or corrected rather than coded from scratch.

nodes.title: Clinician preparing a case for MDT needs a structured summary aligned to pathway requirements and comparable MDT decisions
nodes.description: As a clinician preparing a patient for MDT discussion, I need a structured case summary that reflects the pathway requirements for MDT presentation and includes context from how similar cases were discussed and decided, because manual compilation of MDT summaries from multiple systems is time-consuming and produces inconsistent outputs that slow MDT efficiency.

nodes.title: Clinician reviewing a patient after treatment needs expected recovery markers and comparable recovery trajectories to identify early signals of non-response or recurrence
nodes.description: As a clinician reviewing a patient following treatment, I need to know what the guideline defines as expected recovery markers and how similar patients' recovery trajectories looked, because without structured context early signals of non-response or recurrence can be missed until the patient re-presents with advanced disease.

nodes.title: Avoidable delay assessment with cause classification and impact calculation
nodes.description: The system SHALL provide an avoidable delay assessment capability that analyses clinical episode timelines to identify delays in the patient pathway that were potentially avoidable, classifying each delay by cause category and calculating the impact on overall pathway duration against programme-defined targets.

nodes.title: Downstream products need LEO Core AI clinical outputs exposed as standard FHIR R4 resources conformant to UK Core profiles
nodes.description: As a developer building a downstream Mizaic product, I need LEO Core AI outputs to be consumable as standard FHIR R4 resources so that integration does not require custom adapters and the system can be included in a downstream IEC 62304 system context document.

nodes.title: Operations teams need continuous coding quality monitoring with automated regression alerts
nodes.description: As an operations team member responsible for deployed NLP model quality, I need continuous automated monitoring of coding quality over time with alerts when regressions occur, so that I can act on deteriorating model performance before it affects the quality of patient data and audit outputs.

nodes.title: Clinical safety officers need the review interface to require active evidence engagement to prevent automation bias
nodes.description: As a clinical safety officer responsible for the human review gate, I need the review interface to be designed so that reviewers must actively engage with the clinical evidence before they can confirm an AI recommendation — not just acknowledge it — so that the human review step provides genuine clinical oversight rather than becoming a rubber stamp that automation bias reduces to a single click.

nodes.title: Clinician ordering investigations needs guideline recommendations and comparable ordering patterns to reduce unwarranted variation
nodes.description: As a clinician ordering investigations, I need to see what the guideline recommends at this pathway stage and what investigations were ordered for comparable patients, because without this context investigation ordering varies between clinicians in ways that result in both under-investigation and unnecessary testing.

nodes.title: Audit team leads need completed episodes automatically validated for quality issues before reporting
nodes.description: As an audit team lead, I need completed clinical episodes to be automatically validated for quality issues — duration outliers, missing milestones, temporal anomalies, low-confidence codings, and coding contradictions — so that data quality problems are surfaced and resolved before episodes are used in audit reporting or clinical decisions.

nodes.title: Platform administrators need to configure new audit programmes without code changes
nodes.description: As a platform administrator, I need to configure new clinical audit programmes — including clinical domains, milestone definitions, guideline rule sets, quality targets, and pipeline workflows — through an admin interface without requiring a code change or deployment, so that new programmes can be brought live without involving the engineering team for every configuration update.

nodes.title: Developer implementing authentication needs a standards-compliant auth model with documented token lifecycle and scope definitions
nodes.description: As a developer implementing authentication against LEO Core AI, I need a clear, standards-compliant auth model with documented token lifecycle and scope definitions, so I can implement it consistently across products and satisfy clinical safety and data governance requirements.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need encounter classification rules and model to be manageable and testable via the platform without code changes
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer, I need encounter classification rules and the classification model to be manageable via the platform, so that encounter eligibility decisions for each audit programme are auditable and improvable without code changes.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author managing ODS reference data needs automated weekly synchronisation with mandatory resolution of retired codes before they affect routing or pathway attribution
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author maintaining organisational reference data, I need to identify and resolve ODS changes — trust mergers, PCN reorganisations, site closures, and code retirements — before they cause failures in routing logic, reporting hierarchies, or patient pathway attribution.

nodes.title: Developer building a regulated product on LEO Core AI needs audit documentation and API-level traceability to satisfy their own IEC 62304 and DCB0129 obligations
nodes.description: As a developer building a regulated medical device product on LEO Core AI, I need sufficient documentation and API-level audit support to satisfy my own IEC 62304 and DCB0129 obligations, so that LEO Core AI behaviour can be traced and evidenced within my product's technical file.

nodes.title: System supports SNOMED CT terminology search, resolution, and value set management
nodes.description: Clinical audit teams need to search, browse, and manage SNOMED CT terminology within the platform. This includes hybrid concept resolution (exact match, full-text search, and vector similarity), value set creation and management, concept map maintenance, and writeback of new terminology mappings discovered during the audit process. The terminology service operates against the Coding Neo4j database, separate from patient data.

nodes.title: Clinical content managers need NICE publications automatically ingested and catalogued with coverage status against active pathway rules
nodes.description: As a clinical content manager, I need the system to ingest, catalogue, and tag NICE publications into a searchable internal library so that guideline-to-rule traceability is maintained and the gap between published guidance and implemented rules is always visible.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author tracking NICE output needs structured assessment of Technology Appraisals and Quality Standards with time-bound change requests for mandatory implementation obligations
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author tracking NICE output, I need to assess new and updated Technology Appraisals and Quality Standards for impact on LEO pathway logic, because commissioning obligations and NICE-mandated interventions must be reflected in the system within a timeframe consistent with NHS contractual requirements.

nodes.title: Clinicians need an AI-generated SBAR clinical summary from the coded record for handover and MDT use
nodes.description: As a clinician preparing a patient handover or MDT submission, I need a structured SBAR (Situation-Background-Assessment-Recommendation) summary generated from the coded record, so that critical context is communicated consistently without manual reconstruction from individual encounter notes.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer needs assurance that approved changes are deployed without post-approval modification through an integrity-checked deployment gate
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer, I need assurance that an approved change is deployed exactly as reviewed and that any deviation between the reviewed and deployed state is detected before it reaches a live patient pipeline, so that approval cannot be circumvented by post-approval modification.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer recording a decision needs a structured approval workflow with mandatory rationale, immutable audit record, and hard deployment gate
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer recording a decision, I need to capture a structured, auditable outcome with documented rationale, so that the decision is traceable in the technical file and can withstand post-market surveillance scrutiny.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author managing SNOMED CT alignment needs automated release diffing and a mandatory resolution gate before each new release is activated
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author managing SNOMED CT alignment, I need to assess and integrate each SNOMED CT release against the active LEO concept dictionary, because coding changes in a new release can silently corrupt pathway logic, cohort definitions, and clinical analytics if not assessed and resolved before activation.

nodes.title: Clinical quality reviewers need coded encounters automatically checked against programme guidelines
nodes.description: As a clinical quality reviewer, I need coded encounter data to be automatically evaluated against programme-defined clinical guideline rules, with deviation alerts generated and prioritised by severity, so that guideline non-compliance is surfaced for my attention rather than requiring manual cross-referencing of coded data against guideline criteria.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a proposed change needs a systematic clinical impact assessment to make a defensible approval decision
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer assessing a proposed change, I need to understand the potential clinical impact before making an approval decision, so the decision is defensible and traceable to a documented risk assessment rather than subjective judgement.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need active learning prioritisation, per-entity F1 metrics, golden evaluation set, and warm-start training
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer managing the clinical NER model improvement cycle, I need active learning prioritisation to surface the most informative unlabelled examples first, per-entity F1 metrics from training runs, a frozen golden evaluation set with a blocking quality gate, and warm-start capability from a previously promoted model, so that each training cycle delivers the maximum improvement with the minimum labelling effort.

nodes.title: Clinical content managers need to maintain the ConText assertion rules that determine whether extracted entities are present, absent, or uncertain
nodes.description: As a clinical content manager, I need to maintain the ConText assertion rules that determine whether extracted entities are present, absent, or uncertain, so that assertion accuracy reflects validated clinical linguistic patterns and can be improved without code changes.

nodes.title: Clinical leads need population-level pathway performance dashboards with national benchmark comparison
nodes.description: As a clinical informatician, quality improvement lead, or pathway coordinator, I need visual dashboards showing population-level pathway metrics, waiting time performance, and national benchmarks, so that I can monitor programme performance, identify breaches, and compare outcomes against national findings without building manual reports.

nodes.title: Clinicians need abnormal investigation results and clinical red flags automatically surfaced with a tracked follow-up worklist
nodes.description: As a clinician, I need abnormal investigation results and clinical red flags to be automatically identified and surfaced with a tracked follow-up worklist, so that actionable findings are not missed between consultations.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author managing ICD-10 and OPCS alignment needs structured release diffing with separate mandatory sign-off for secondary uses data mappings
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author maintaining diagnostic and procedure coding alignment, I need to assess NHS Digital ICD-10 and OPCS updates against active coding mappings, because changes to procedure codes or diagnostic categories can introduce errors into pathway logic and secondary uses data submissions if not assessed and resolved before activation.

nodes.title: Clinical content managers need AI-assisted extraction of structured pathway decision rules from guideline text with mandatory clinical reviewer approval
nodes.description: As a clinical content manager, I need AI-assisted extraction of structured decision rules from guideline text so that pathway logic is derived from authoritative sources with full provenance, rather than being authored from memory.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author needs a structured authoring environment with mandatory source traceability and staged release control for every guideline entry
nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author authoring an update to the internal guideline library, I need a structured authoring environment that enforces traceability to the source document and prevents unreviewed content from entering the active library, because every version of every guideline must be evidenced back to its authoritative source in the technical file.

nodes.title: NLP engineers need automated AI-assisted auditing of training labels with safe auto-fix and human review routing
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer or clinical AI team member, I need an automated system that audits training label records for quality issues — assertion errors, label inconsistencies, SNOMED coding problems, and value or unit mismatches — and applies safe fixes automatically while routing SNOMED issues to human review, so that label quality is maintained at scale without requiring manual inspection of every record.

nodes.title: Data protection leads need patient identifiers automatically removed from clinical text before transmission to external AI services
nodes.description: As a data protection officer or information governance lead responsible for patient data transmitted to external AI services, I need the system to automatically strip or replace all direct patient identifiers from clinical free text before it is sent to any external LLM API, so that personal health data is not transmitted to a third-party processor beyond what is strictly necessary for the clinical purpose.

nodes.title: Clinical teams need to define and manage patient cohorts by clinical and demographic criteria for audit, research, and benchmarking
nodes.description: As a quality improvement lead, I need to define and manage named patient cohorts using clinical and demographic inclusion/exclusion criteria, so that audit programmes, research missions, and benchmark comparisons can be scoped to the right population consistently and repeatably.

nodes.title: Any clinician-facing output must surface the completeness and reliability of the underlying data before a decision is made
nodes.description: As a clinician receiving AI-generated informational context, I need to know how complete and reliable the underlying data is before I use it to inform a clinical decision, because incomplete or unrepresentative data presented without disclosure could lead me to draw incorrect conclusions and act in ways that harm the patient.

nodes.title: Platform administrators need configuration validation and test mode before activating pipeline changes
nodes.description: As a platform administrator setting up or updating a pipeline configuration for a tenant, I need a test mode that runs the complete configured pipeline against a sample input before activation, so that misconfiguration is caught and visible before the configuration processes real patient records.

nodes.title: Developer handling integration failures needs a structured, consistent error response schema with sufficient diagnostic information
nodes.description: As a developer handling failures in a LEO Core AI integration, I need a structured, consistent error response schema with sufficient diagnostic information, so I can implement appropriate error handling without needing to reverse-engineer failure modes through trial and error.

nodes.title: Mizaic clinical reviewer needs a structured change queue with risk-prioritised triage so nothing unapproved reaches a live patient pipeline
nodes.description: As a Mizaic clinical reviewer, I need a structured queue of pending changes with sufficient context to prioritise review workload, so that high-risk changes are assessed before lower-risk ones and nothing awaiting approval silently affects a live pipeline.

nodes.title: Clinician reviewing a referral needs pathway criteria and comparable referral outcomes to support consistent triage decisions
nodes.description: As a clinician reviewing an incoming referral, I need to see the relevant pathway eligibility criteria and how similar referrals were triaged and managed, because without this context triage decisions rely on individual recall of guidelines and vary between clinicians in ways that affect patient safety.

nodes.title: Operations teams need a real-time dashboard showing pipeline throughput, queue status, and data quality indicators across all active programmes
nodes.description: As an operations team member, I need a real-time operational dashboard showing pipeline throughput, episode build status, encounter processing queues, and DQ indicators across all active programmes, so that failures and quality regressions are detected and actioned before they affect audit outputs.

nodes.title: AI engineering teams need every coding override categorised by error type for model improvement
nodes.description: As an NLP engineer or clinical AI team member, I need every human override or correction of an AI coding proposal to be recorded with a structured error category — not just that an override occurred, but why — so that model weaknesses can be identified systematically from real reviewer decisions and addressed in the training cycle rather than through anecdote.

nodes.title: Developer integrating long-running operations needs a consistent async job pattern with predictable status lifecycle and notification options
nodes.description: As a developer integrating long-running LEO Core AI operations, I need a consistent, documented async job pattern with predictable status lifecycle and webhook or polling options, so I can build resilient product workflows without custom workarounds for each operation type.

nodes.title: Operations teams need automated detection of longitudinal drift in coding patterns with root cause labelling and escalating alerts
nodes.description: As an operations team member, I need automated detection of longitudinal drift in audit coding patterns so that systematic model degradation or clinical practice changes are identified and escalated before they corrupt trend reporting.

nodes.title: Experienced clinicians with age-related vision, hearing, or dexterity changes can use LEO at full professional speed
nodes.description: Primary care is staffed by clinicians across the full adult age range, including partners in their 60s and 70s and returners working reduced hours. These users are highly expert but their interface needs differ from younger users: larger default text, generous target sizes, high-contrast options, no thin strokes, no low-contrast grey-on-grey, no time-pressured interactions, no animations that distract, and a keyboard-first option for every mouse gesture. They are also the product most senior reviewers and safety owners. If LEO is unpleasant or tiring for them, clinical oversight suffers. An explicit persona makes these needs testable.

nodes.title: Clinical reviewers need plain-language AI interpretation of coded audit findings
nodes.description: As a clinical reviewer working through a coded episode or audit alert, I need the system to generate a plain-language interpretation of what the coded data shows clinically, so that I can quickly understand the significance of a finding without needing to interpret raw SNOMED codes and interval calculations myself.

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Author needs automated alerting when authoritative guideline sources publish updates relevant to LEO-managed pathways
