nodes.description: As a Knowledge Base Author responsible for the currency and integrity of clinical content in LEO Core AI, I need to be alerted when an authoritative guideline source publishes an update relevant to a LEO-managed pathway, because content drift in a regulated medical device is a patient safety risk and the internal guideline library must not silently diverge from the current evidence base between active monitoring cycles.

nodes.title: Pathway coordinators need pathway intervals automatically calculated against programme waiting time targets
nodes.description: As a pathway coordinator or clinical lead, I need pathway intervals and duration metrics automatically calculated against programme-defined waiting time targets, so that I can identify breaches and delays across a patient population without manually performing date arithmetic across multiple records.

nodes.title: Clinical informaticians need a guided research workspace to investigate populations and analyse pathway bottlenecks without data science skills
nodes.description: As a clinical informatician, audit team lead, or pathway coordinator, I need a guided research workspace where I can investigate patient populations, discover cohorts, and analyse pathway bottlenecks by selecting from plain-English mission cards and answering a small number of scoping questions, so that I can conduct meaningful population-level analysis without needing data science skills or knowledge of the underlying graph algorithms.

nodes.title: Centralised test patient library: data shape, cross-graph copy, redaction, SBAR seed, dialog wiring, per-aspect editor, AI authoring AND SBAR / referral triage surfacing (relabel + outcome filter + NG12 backfill)
nodes.description: Hermetic verification of the test patient library across Phase A (data shape + cross-graph copy + SBAR seed + dialog wiring), Phase B (per-aspect editor), the two AI-assisted authoring flows (flow 1 scaffold-from-rule, flow 2 author-from-scenario), and the SBAR / referral triage surfacing work (relabel the 'summarisation' aspect to 'SBAR / referral triage' to make NG12 referral triage scope explicit; add a triage-outcome chip filter visible only on the SBAR aspect that shows counts per outcome (2ww, urgent, routine, no rule fired, evaluator outage, unset) and lets the reviewer narrow the table; backfill the SBAR golden set with 7 NG12 suspected-cancer pathways (bladder, endometrial, melanoma, pancreatic, head and neck, prostate, sarcoma) plus 2 adversarial 'red flag word but criteria not met' cases (haematuria with active UTI in patient under 45; pigmented lesion with 7-point checklist score 1) so the rule engine is held to NG12 coverage AND to the negative cases that reject premature 2WW escalation). New fixtures whose rules are not yet seeded in the rule engine are explicitly marked draft: true so the runner skips structural assertions on them and counts them as drafts in the run summary -- this keeps the test honest (no silent failures) without blocking the backfill on parallel rule-engine work.

nodes.title: System processes pipeline runs within acceptable time limits and scales to multiple organisations
nodes.description: All users need the system to process pipeline runs within acceptable time limits. A full audit pipeline for a single patient should complete within 2 minutes. The system must scale horizontally to handle multiple organisations running concurrent pipeline jobs. Infrastructure must support auto-scaling based on queue depth and maintain availability of 99.5% during business hours.

nodes.title: System provides electronic safety-netting for patients with cancer-relevant symptoms
nodes.description: Pathway coordinators need electronic safety-netting tools that identify patients who presented with cancer-relevant symptoms but were not referred or investigated within expected timeframes. The system shall flag patients where there is a gap between symptom presentation and expected follow-up action, enabling proactive outreach. This supports the Network Contract DES requirement for strengthening and standardising safety netting, including the use of electronic tools.

nodes.title: Referral management administrators need the system to ingest incoming referrals from all channels into a single unified queue
nodes.description: Referrals currently arrive through multiple channels. e-RS is the primary NHS channel, but email referrals, posted letters, faxed letters, and in some cases direct EHR-to-EHR referrals also occur. Each channel requires a different monitoring process. Referrals arriving outside e-RS are not automatically visible to the referral management team and can sit undetected in a generic email inbox for days. Even within e-RS, referrals may be directed to wrong mailboxes or departments. The system must provide adapters for each major referral channel that extract the referral content, normalise it to a standard internal format, and place it in the unified queue within a defined time limit from arrival. Channel of origin must be recorded with every referral for audit purposes.

nodes.title: System imports patient records via FHIR R4 and exports audit results as FHIR resources
nodes.description: System administrators need the system to import patient encounter records via FHIR R4 APIs (Encounter, DocumentReference, Patient resources) from GP clinical systems. The system must also export audit results as FHIR resources including Measure (audit programme definitions), MeasureReport (programme results), and Device (system identity). FHIR compliance enables integration with NHS Digital infrastructure and interoperability with other audit tools.

nodes.title: Audit and coding staff see every task they need to action in one unified queue
nodes.description: Audit and coding staff today open at least five screens to do a full day work: the coding-review queue, the safety-net alerts list, the gold-label review queue, the surface-form review queue, and the audit-run inbox. They tell us the commonest question at stand-up is where do I pick up from yesterday. The user need: a single /work route that, for the staff role, is the app landing page. It lists every open task the user is responsible for, grouped by task type but displayed as one ordered queue. Each row says what the task is, why it is urgent, and which action resolves it. Filters let staff focus on a specific source (coding, safety, gold) without losing visibility of the others.

userNeed.title: LEO presents each user the slimmest viable experience for their role
userNeed.description: LEO serves four very different working lives from the same app: a clinician opening a patient record between appointments, a coding or audit staff member working a queue of tasks, a QA/RA lead investigating the product own behaviour, and a platform admin looking after tenants and users. Today the nav shows the same long list to everyone. Junior staff and older clinicians in particular tell us the app feels like it is for someone else and that the extra choice slows them down. The user need: on first sign-in the user picks a role once. After that, the app lands them on the right home screen, shows a short nav for their role, and tucks the rest behind a single Advanced tray. A user with more than one role can switch from a clearly labelled switcher in the top right. Switching role never hides clinical data; it only changes emphasis and layout.

designInputs.title: Role-first shell rollout cleanup (flag removal, duplicates, lint)
designInputs.description: Once the role-first shell is the shipped default, the repository SHALL be cleaned of the rollout scaffolding and legacy duplicates so no developer accidentally re-introduces the old layout. Concretely: (a) the NEXT_PUBLIC_ROLE_FIRST feature flag and every code-side branch on it SHALL be removed; (b) the duplicate ProgressiveReveal component at services/ui/src/components/ui/ProgressiveReveal.tsx SHALL be deleted and its callers migrated to @leo/design-system; (c) the Google Fonts @import at the top of services/ui/src/app/globals.css SHALL be removed; (d) a lint rule SHALL flag new hex/rgb/hsl colour literals written inside an MUI sx prop so reviewers steer contributors toward colour tokens.

designInputs.title: RoleGate, RolePicker, RoleSwitcher primitives with feature-flagged role-first shell
designInputs.description: The system SHALL provide three primitives in @leo/design-system: (1) RoleGate context provider that exposes the current role, allowed roles, and a switchRole() function; (2) RolePicker modal shown on first load when selected_role is null; (3) RoleSwitcher control that appears in the app shell for multi-role users. The app shell SHALL filter left-nav items based on the active role's primary set, with demoted items placed inside a single Advanced tray. A feature flag SHALL allow the role-first shell to be rolled out independently.

designInputs.title: Centralised MUI theme factory (createLeoTheme) sourced from design-system tokens
designInputs.description: The MUI theme used by services/ui SHALL be produced by a factory function (createLeoTheme) exported from @leo/design-system/theme, not by a theme object defined inside services/ui. The factory SHALL consume its palette, typography, and shape values from the design-system tokens in services/design-system/src/tokens/* so that a single change to a token propagates to every MUI component and every role-first surface.

designInputs.title: Motion layer with framer-motion and prefers-reduced-motion gating
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single motion layer built on framer-motion, with pre-canned transitions (default 180 ms ease-out, 220 ms spring for route change, 120 ms for hover and focus). All motion SHALL be gated by the browser's prefers-reduced-motion media query so users who have requested reduced motion receive an instant state change with no animation.

designInputs.title: Single @leo/design-system workspace package for tokens, primitives, motion, copy
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single design-system workspace package (@leo/design-system) that owns tokens (colour, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, density), primitives (shell, role gate, knowledge page, stat hero, progressive reveal, task queue), motion infra, and role-scoped copy. All UI services SHALL import from this package; no service SHALL ship duplicated local copies of these concerns.

designInputs.title: DM Sans typography via next/font with humanist sans for clinical labels
designInputs.description: The system SHALL load DM Sans via next/font/google (preload, subset, self-hosted) and use it for all body, heading, and subtitle typography. Monospace (JetBrains Mono) SHALL be reserved for <code>, <kbd>, and raw SNOMED identifiers; subtitle1 and subtitle2 variants SHALL switch from mono to DM Sans 600.

designOutputs.title: services/design-system as npm workspace package '@leo/design-system'
designOutputs.description: Introduces a root package.json declaring workspaces, a new services/design-system package, and updates services/ui to consume it via transpilePackages + a TypeScript path alias. The package owns tokens, motion, fonts, primitives, roles, and copy helpers.

designOutputs.title: Role-first shell primitives + feature flag
designOutputs.description: Adds @leo/design-system/roles exporting RoleContext, RoleProvider, RoleGate, RolePicker, RoleSwitcher, useRole(), and a navMap. AppShell wraps its children in RoleProvider and filters its left nav by the active role when the feature flag NEXT_PUBLIC_ROLE_FIRST is 'on'.

designOutputs.title: createLeoTheme() factory in @leo/design-system consumed by services/ui ThemeRegistry
designOutputs.description: The MUI theme moves out of services/ui into the shared design-system workspace package. A single exported factory, createLeoTheme, reads tokens from services/design-system/src/ tokens/color, /spacing, and /typography and returns a complete MUI Theme. services/ui/src/components/ThemeRegistry.tsx imports the factory from "@leo/design-system/theme" and instantiates it once; the old services/ui/src/theme.ts file is removed. The design-system package.json exposes the new path via its exports map so consumers can import it without reaching into src/. Static-analysis tests are updated to read the new location.

designOutputs.title: next/font DM Sans + subtitle1/2 un-monospaced
designOutputs.description: Adds @leo/design-system/fonts that exports dmSans and jetBrainsMono loaders configured via next/font/google. services/ui/src/app/layout.tsx applies dmSans.className. Theme typography updated so subtitle1 and subtitle2 use DM Sans 600 instead of JetBrains Mono.

designOutputs.title: MotionProvider, useMotion, and pre-canned transitions
designOutputs.description: Adds framer-motion as a services/ui dependency. Introduces @leo/design-system/motion exporting MotionProvider and useMotion() that returns { reducedMotion, transitions }. Transitions collapse to duration 0 when reducedMotion is true.

designOutputs.title: Role-first rollout flag removed; duplicate primitives deleted; font @import removed; sx colour-literal lint rule added
designOutputs.description: Closing move for Wave D. The NEXT_PUBLIC_ROLE_FIRST flag is physically removed from next.config.mjs, RoleShellProvider, and AppShell -- the role-first shell is the only codepath. The duplicate MUI-backed ProgressiveReveal in components/ui/ is deleted in favour of the design-system primitive. The Google Fonts @import that predated next/font is removed from globals.css (DM Sans + JetBrains Mono already load via next/font/google). eslint.config.mjs now carries a no-restricted-syntax rule that flags hex / rgb / hsl colour literals inside JSX sx props so new contributions stay on the token system.

userNeed.title: Platform must enforce physical database-level separation of patient data between tenants with automated provisioning and deprovision
userNeed.description: As a platform administrator, I need the system to enforce physical separation of patient data between tenants so that a misconfiguration or access error in one tenant cannot expose patient records from another.

designInputs.title: Multi-tenancy: dedicated Neo4j patient graph per tenant with automated provisioning
designInputs.description: The system SHALL assign each tenant a dedicated Neo4j patient graph instance with no shared patient data nodes, and SHALL provide an automated provisioning script that creates the dedicated instance, credentials, and Key Vault secrets as an idempotent operation.

designInputs.title: Multi-tenancy: tenant token validation before query execution with architecturally enforced single-driver scoping
designInputs.description: The system SHALL validate the tenant context token on every API request before any Cypher query executes, return a 401 for missing or invalid tokens, and construct all Cypher query builders to accept only a single driver connection scoped to the requesting tenant, with cross-tenant access verified as architecturally impossible by automated test.

designOutputs.title: Card-based Operations UX
designOutputs.description: Replaces tabbed /admin/operations with a card dashboard and a dedicated /admin/operations/reviews workflow page. Labels are plain-language and suitable for low reading-age accessibility.

designOutputs.title: Authentication and Authorisation Module
designOutputs.description: Provides authentication and authorisation for all API endpoints. Validates Entra ID (Azure AD) tokens, enforces organisation-scoped tenancy, and manages service-to-service authentication between internal microservices. Injects tenant context into request dependencies for data isolation.

designOutputs.title: Surface-form validation and tasking
designOutputs.description: Adds a surface_form_validation subgraph after terminology resolution. High-confidence corrections are auto-applied; low-confidence mismatches create SurfaceFormTask items for human approval. Extends admin gold-dataset operations with manual candidate dedupe preview/apply controls for near-duplicate training examples.

designOutputs.title: Auth, role-state and tenant-scope middleware
designOutputs.description:
Design output documenting the authN/authZ surface: `libs/auth/role_state.py` (RoleState, canonical role set, selected-role workflow), `libs/auth/tenant_context.py` (tenant scope), `libs/auth/practitioner_org_context.py` (clinician-org binding), `libs/auth/service_auth.py`, `libs/auth/org_scope.py`, and `services/api/app/routers/auth.py`. Gaps (batch-15 Theme B/C): formalised token lifecycle documentation (UN-A031A603), explicit conflict-of-interest attestation artefact per review (UN-17724530), and physical database-level tenant separation (UN-412D1ECD currently implemented as logical tenant-scoped Cypher rather than per-tenant DB). Backlogged.

userNeed.title: Per-episode specialist visit attribution without cross-pathway contamination
userNeed.description: Clinical quality managers and auditors need each cancer investigation episode to carry only the specialist visit that genuinely belongs to it. When a patient has multiple cancer referral episodes sharing the same cancer site (e.g. two breast 2WW referrals in different years), a specialist clinic visit from the first pathway must not be attributed to the second. Incorrect attribution produces false stale_post_specialist episode counts, inflated specialist-seen rates, and inaccurate NCDA audit metrics.

designInputs.title: Per-episode temporal claiming of specialist visit anchors
designInputs.description: The episode detection system SHALL attribute each specialist visit anchor to at most one EpisodeOfCare node using a per-episode temporal claiming algorithm. A specialist visit is eligible for an episode only if (a) its encounter date is on or after the episode referral date, (b) its encounter date is on or before the episode window end date (diagnosis date for closed episodes; referral_date + 365 days for open episodes), and (c) its cancer site key is compatible with the episode site key. Episodes are processed in referral-date order (earliest first) so that earlier pathways have priority over later pathways when multiple episodes share a site key. Each visit that is successfully claimed is removed from the pool and cannot be attributed to any other episode.

designOutputs.title: Per-episode specialist visit claiming algorithm
designOutputs.description: Replaces the global-per-site-key _group_specialists function with a per-episode claiming algorithm implemented as _claim_specialists_for_episodes.  Algorithm: 1. Sort all specialist visit anchors ascending by encounter_date. 2. Build _EpisodeSpec for each episode (ep_id, site_key, ref_date, window_end).    - Closed episodes: window_end = diagnosis date (latest encounter in group).    - Open episodes: window_end = ref_date + 365 days. 3. Process episodes in ref_date ascending order. 4. For each episode, find the earliest unclaimed specialist visit where:    - site key is compatible (_site_keys_compatible)    - encounter_date >= ref_date    - encounter_date <= window_end 5. Claim the visit (mark index as used); store _SpecialistClaim on episode. 6. Episodes with no matching visit receive _SpecialistClaim(specialist_seen=False).  _write_episode now accepts a _SpecialistClaim directly instead of dicts, eliminating the dict.get(site_key) lookup that previously allowed one dict entry to supply data to multiple episodes.

designOutputs.title: Admin Guard and ReDoS-Safe Regex Validation in Training Router
designOutputs.description: Hardened services/api/app/routers/training.py implementing four security controls for clinical rule mutation endpoints:  1. ADMIN-ONLY ACCESS: All four mutation endpoints now carry    Depends(require_admin) as a FastAPI parameter dependency:      - POST   /training/post-processor-rules      - PATCH  /training/post-processor-rules/{rule_id}      - POST   /training/context-rules      - PATCH  /training/context-rules/{rule_id}/deactivate    Non-admin requests return HTTP 403 before any business logic runs.  2. REDOS-SAFE REGEX VALIDATION: _validate_regex(pattern, max_length=200)    is called for all user-supplied context_regex inputs:      - Length check: > 200 chars -> HTTP 422      - Syntax check: re.compile() failure -> HTTP 422      - ReDoS probe: subprocess.run() with two pathological probe strings        (_REDOS_PROBE_LOWER = "a"*38, _REDOS_PROBE_SIMPLE = "a"*50+"b")        and 0.5s OS-level timeout -> HTTP 422 on TimeoutExpired  3. LITERAL VALIDATION: ConText rule literals capped at 200 characters;    empty strings rejected with HTTP 422.  4. AUDIT TRAIL HARDENING: created_by is always set from scope.email    (server-verified session identity), never from the request body.

designOutputs.title: Canonical relation schema, policy validation, relation train/eval, and model-first runtime linking
designOutputs.description: This output implements a first-class relation path across API, UI, training, and runtime:  1. Canonical relation persistence:    - Gold label entity payloads persist relations[] rows with      type/target_idx/target_text/confidence.    - Legacy body-site fields are mirrored for backward compatibility.  2. Ontology policy:    - Shared relation policy matrix defines allowed source/target semantic      label pairs and relation families.    - API and runtime use the same policy checks.  3. Gold review UX:    - Multi-site relation picker supports one source term linked to multiple      body-structure targets.    - Recommendation panel ranks ontology-valid links and supports accept,      reject, and undo actions.  4. Relation model training path:    - relation_exporter emits relation_train.jsonl and relation_dev.jsonl.    - relation_trainer learns label-pair priors and writes relation_model.json.    - relation_evaluator reports precision/recall/F1 and per-type metrics.    - job_runner integrates relation export/train/eval into the training job.  5. Runtime relation linking:    - relation_linking subgraph predicts relations model-first and calls LLM      fallback only for low-confidence coverage.    - persisted relation rows are canonicalized and deduplicated.

userNeed.title: Engineering leads need the platform to follow Mizaic standard architecture and engineering design principles consistently across all services
userNeed.description: As an engineering lead responsible for the LEO Core AI platform, I need all services to follow Mizaic's standard architecture and engineering design principles consistently — workflow-as-data, configuration-as-data, async fire-and-track, AI models as graph nodes, secrets from Key Vault, and enforced code quality limits — so that any engineer can onboard to any part of the codebase with predictable patterns, and the system remains maintainable and auditable as it grows.

designInputs.title: Async fire-and-track job pattern with consistent status model for all long-running operations
designInputs.description: The system SHALL implement a consistent async fire-and-track pattern for all long-running operations, with 202 responses, job_id-based polling, persistent job state, and a uniform status model across all operation types.

designInputs.title: All secrets retrieved exclusively from Azure Key Vault with CI secret scanning and startup failure on missing secrets
designInputs.description: The system SHALL retrieve all secrets exclusively from Azure Key Vault using DefaultAzureCredential; no secrets SHALL appear in source code, committed environment files, or container images; services SHALL exit on secret retrieval failure.

designInputs.title: Unified LangGraph coding agent as the single execution path for all coding and pipeline jobs
designInputs.description: The system SHALL use a single unified LangGraph-based coding and audit agent as the exclusive runtime execution path for all clinical coding and pipeline jobs, with the training and runtime pipelines sharing the same post-processing functions, so that there is no divergence between paths and all coding outputs are traceable to a single versioned agent definition.

designInputs.title: CI-enforced code quality gates: black, flake8, ESLint with function and file length limits
designInputs.description: The system SHALL enforce automated code quality checks in CI: black formatting and flake8 linting for Python, ESLint for TypeScript, with function and file length limits; any violation blocks the merge pipeline.

designInputs.title: All pipeline and workflow logic defined as graph data and executed by a single generic executor
designInputs.description: The system SHALL define all pipeline and workflow logic as graph data stored as WorkflowDefinition and WorkflowStep nodes in the primary database, and SHALL execute all workflows through a single generic executor that reads step definitions at runtime, so that new workflows and pipeline configurations can be added by inserting graph data without any code changes or deployments.

designInputs.title: AI model configurations stored as graph nodes with runtime resolution and no hardcoded model names
designInputs.description: The system SHALL store all AI model configurations as AIModel nodes in the graph database and SHALL resolve model parameters at runtime from these nodes; no model names or provider parameters SHALL be hardcoded in application code.

designOutputs.title: NICE Syndication API Client and Guideline Ingest Pipeline
designOutputs.description: Three-file implementation providing: async NICE API client with Redis-cached guideline catalogue; idempotent Neo4j upsert of Guideline, Recommendation, and Section nodes; FastAPI router with catalogue search, fire-and-track ingest, SSE progress stream, and job status endpoints. No LLM anywhere in this pipeline.

designOutputs.title: Programme Configuration Registry
designOutputs.description: Manages clinical audit programme configurations as graph data in Neo4j. Supports creation, validation, activation, and deactivation of programme configurations including clinical domain definitions, milestone types, guideline rule sets, quality targets, and pipeline workflow definitions. All programme-specific logic is stored as data, not code, enabling new audit programmes to be deployed through configuration changes only.

designOutputs.title: Unified Pipeline Worker Service
designOutputs.description: A single worker service that consumes from the pipeline-jobs queue, processes unified PipelineJobMessage payloads, and executes pipeline steps by dispatching to the appropriate subgraph handlers. Replaces separate coding_worker and analysis_worker job handlers with one unified service backed by LangGraph and FHIR PlanDefinition-driven orchestration.

designOutputs.title: Platform architecture, AI model registry, and CI quality gates
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-2C6E6933 platform foundations. Components: libs/pipeline_graph LangGraph-style executor and tool registry (DI-A90B19EB, DI-3FDBB57B), Neo4j-stored AI model registry and prompt templates (DI-2C56591B), Azure Key Vault secrets handling via config loader (DI-6EBF12F1), .github/workflows CI pipelines running black + flake8 (DI-932C270C), code-quality.mdc function-length enforcement (DI-693FFEEA). Code-gap flagged: automated function-length CI check not yet wired; currently enforced by review.

Queries Knowledge Graph for concept FSN, semantic_tag, and      collect(sf.form) (existing aliases) using GET_CONCEPT_FOR_SUGGESTION.   2. User prompt includes concept FSN, SNOMED ID, semantic tag, and      existing aliases (no patient data, no encounter text).   5. Parses JSON array from LLM response using re.search.   6. Filters out suggestions already in existing_aliases (case-insensitive).   7. Returns up to 10 suggestions: {suggestions: [...], concept_id: ...}   8. Privacy guarantee: only concept metadata is transmitted to the LLM. The Cypher query (GET_CONCEPT_FOR_SUGGESTION) selects c.fsn, c.semantic_tag, and collect(sf.form) only.  -- 2. userNeed.title: Clinical reviewers and auditors need every AI-extracted entity linked to its source text phrase with immutable provenance
userNeed.description: As a clinical reviewer, clinical coder, or auditor working with AI-extracted clinical codes, I need every extracted entity to link back to the exact phrase in the source text that generated it, with the extraction method, confidence score, and assertion context visible alongside it, so that I can verify each extraction in seconds without reading the full source document, and so that a complete evidence chain exists for every coded finding.

designInputs.title: Audit trail API providing provenance access without clinical record exposure
designInputs.description: The system SHALL provide a dedicated audit trail API endpoint that returns extraction provenance records, assertion evidence, and correction events for authorised auditors without exposing the underlying clinical record free-text or patient identifiable data.

designInputs.title: Provenance record immutable retention policy enforcement (7-year minimum)
designInputs.description: The system SHALL retain all extraction provenance records in an immutable, append-only store for a minimum of 7 years from the date of creation, and SHALL enforce a write-once policy that rejects any update or delete operation on a provenance record within the retention window.

designInputs.title: Absolute character-offset resolver for LLM-extracted entities
designInputs.description: The extraction pipeline SHALL resolve absolute character offsets (span_start, span_end) for every LLM-extracted entity against the original encounter text, honouring sentence boundaries and repeated mentions, so that every extracted entity has immutable provenance back to its source phrase.

designInputs.title: Assertion evidence text context stored alongside assertion label
designInputs.description: The system SHALL store alongside each assertion label the verbatim text window that the assertion model evaluated to determine that label, so that a reviewer can read the textual evidence for the assertion without needing to re-read the full source document.

designInputs.title: Reviewer correction event schema immutably linked to extraction provenance
designInputs.description: The system SHALL record every reviewer coding correction as an immutable event appended to the extraction provenance record, containing the original code, replacement code, correction rationale, reviewer identity and role, and timestamp.

designInputs.title: Clinical qualifier preservation in LLM extraction for SNOMED specificity
designInputs.description: The LLM extraction prompt (extraction_v1) SHALL instruct the model to preserve clinical qualifiers - laterality, severity, acuity, episodicity, morphology, anatomical site, and temporal qualifiers - in the extracted term text and in the lookup_term field used for SNOMED terminology retrieval. Qualifiers SHALL NOT be stripped to a canonical headword when the source narrative contains them.

designInputs.title: Source-text highlight linking for reviewer entity selection
designInputs.description: The system SHALL render the source clinical text for each extracted entity when a reviewer selects that entity, with the specific character span that generated the entity highlighted; the highlight SHALL correspond exactly to the character offsets stored in the provenance record.

designInputs.title: Immutable source-span linkage and provenance for extracted entities
designInputs.description: Each AI-extracted entity SHALL store the exact source text span, model or rule identifier, confidence, assertion context, and an integrity hash that rejects post-hoc edits.

designOutputs.title: Ambiguous GP Abbreviation Disambiguation Rules
designOutputs.description: Three-layer defence against miscoding of ambiguous GP abbreviations:  Layer 1 - Extraction prompt (libs/prompts/extraction_v1.py):   - "CA" alone added to DO NOT EXTRACT list; requires organ/site context.   - "MSK" alone added to DO NOT EXTRACT list; only specific symptom coded.   - NAD disambiguation note: always tag as finding, never substance.   - Abbreviation expansion table extended with 30+ new entries covering     cancer pathway, chronic conditions, symptoms, and investigations.   - CRITICAL disambiguation block added after abbreviation table.  Layer 2 - Escalation prompts (libs/llm_client/escalation.py):   - Rule 10 added to escalate_coding() prompt: CA/MSK/NAD guidance.   - Rule 11 added to _CANDIDATES_SYSTEM: same guidance for ask-leo path.   - Both prompts updated in the same changeset (dual-path parity).  Layer 3 - Resolver concept blocklist (libs/terminology/client.py):   - _ABBREV_BLOCKED_CONCEPTS dict maps normalised abbreviation text     to a set of SNOMED concept IDs that are incorrect in GP context.   - _filter_abbrev_noise() applied during re-keying in both     TerminologyClient.resolve() and AsyncTerminologyClient.resolve_raw().   - Blocked for "nad": 104695007, 124316006, 131143000 (NAD biochemistry).  Surface form writeback:   - 43 abbreviation surface forms written to terminology server with     confidence 1.0 and provenance "abbreviation_audit_april_2026".   - 3 review-required entries (TWOC, OOH, NAD) subsequently resolved     and written after clinic

designOutputs.title: LLM extractor v2 (prompt + ExtractedTerm/ExtractionItem parser)
designOutputs.description: Updated extraction prompt (libs/prompts/extraction_v1.py) with new CLINICAL QUALIFIER PRESERVATION, ASSERTION, and CONFIDENCE sections. Updated parsers in services/coding_worker/app/pipeline/llm_extractor.py and libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/_extractor.py to parse, normalise, and clamp assertion and confidence, resolve absolute spans via SpanResolver, and propagate the new fields onto ExtractedTerm and ExtractionItem records. Added _normalise_assertion and _normalise_confidence helpers.

designOutputs.title: SpanResolver -- absolute character-offset resolver for LLM-extracted terms
designOutputs.description: Shared utility that resolves absolute ``(span_start, span_end)`` offsets for LLM-extracted terms within the full encounter text. Maintains per-sentence and encounter-wide cursors so repeated mentions of the same surface form get distinct offsets. Falls back to encounter-wide search when a sentence-scoped match fails.

designOutputs.title: SpanResolver utility (libs/ner/span_resolver.py)
designOutputs.description: New shared utility class SpanResolver that resolves absolute character (start, end) offsets for LLM-extracted terms within an encounter. Uses sentence-level and encounter-wide cursors to disambiguate repeated mentions. Consumed by both services/coding_worker/app/pipeline/llm_extractor.py and libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs/_extractor.py so both LLM extractor code paths produce accurate spans.

designOutputs.title: Audit-Driven Automated Encounter Remediation
designOutputs.description: A Python script and supporting Cypher query module that reads the audit SQLite checkpoint, groups findings by encounter, fetches encounter text and current DOCUMENTS from Neo4j, submits all proposed changes for each encounter to Claude Sonnet for independent verification, and applies confirmed changes (agree=true, confidence >= 0.80) to Neo4j. Changes below threshold are written to a disputes log.  Three action types are supported:   delete -- removes an overcoded DOCUMENTS relationship (and patient             shortcut if no other encounter codes the concept)   add    -- resolves the snomed_search term via terminology API and             creates a new DOCUMENTS relationship with the correct             assertion and evidence   update_assertion -- updates the assertion field on an existing             DOCUMENTS relationship  A SQLite remediation table provides idempotency and the audit trail.

designOutputs.title: first_seen milestone: anchor detector + episode builder wiring
designOutputs.description: Adds a first_seen milestone bucket to the anchor detector text-search layer and wires it through the episode builder so that IS_PART_OF edges with milestone_type='first_seen' are written for fast-track/2WW clinic attendance encounters, and a first_seen_date property is stored on the EpisodeOfCare node. Also lowers MIN_REFERRAL_TO_DIAG_DAYS from 3 to 0 to capture same-day PRISM-pathway referrals (one-stop breast/dermatology clinics).

designOutputs.title: Stage-at-diagnosis enrichment modules and audit surfacing
designOutputs.description: Implements a first-class stage-at-diagnosis capability: rule ingestion from NHS staging-sheet outputs, TNM parser, deterministic staging engine, post-episode enrichment subgraph, EpisodeOfCare staging fields, analytics aggregation, and audit UI rendering of early/late distribution plus source and coverage.

designOutputs.title: Spinal-TNM scope guard and LLM prompt disambiguation rule
designOutputs.description: Two coordinated changes that form a dual-layer defence against spinal vertebral notation being misclassified as cancer TNM staging:  Layer 1 -- LLM prompt (extraction_v1.py):   A new negative extraction rule in the DO NOT EXTRACT section instructs   the extraction model not to label isolated vertebral level tokens (C1-C7,   T1-T12, L1-L5, S1-S5) as staging scale or observable entity when the   sentence contains spinal anatomical or physiotherapy context signals.  Layer 2 -- Post-processing scope guard (scope_guard.py):   A new is_spinal_context() predicate and a matching check block inside   reclassify_assertion(). When a standalone TNM component token (T0-T4,   N0-N3, M0-M1 with optional c/p/y/r prefix) appears in a sentence with   spinal markers and no full TNM triplet, reclassify_assertion() returns   SUPPRESSED. The _apply_scope_guard_to_dicts() caller in post_processing.py   removes the entity before terminology resolution.

designOutputs.title: LLM extractor paths updated for span resolution, self-rated assertion, self-rated confidence, and clinical-qualifier preservation
designOutputs.description: Both LLM extractor implementations (the coding_worker extractor and the WorkflowEngine subgraph extractor) are updated to:  - Call the shared SpanResolver (DO-LEO-AI-110) so every extracted   term carries accurate absolute character offsets into the   encounter text. - Parse the LLM's emitted ``assertion`` value into the   ExtractionItem / ExtractedTerm assertion field, clamping to the   controlled vocabulary and defaulting to ``present`` when missing. - Parse the LLM's self-rated ``confidence`` in [0, 1], clamping to   valid range and defaulting to 1.0 when missing. - Receive updated system prompt instructions that tell the LLM to   preserve clinical qualifiers (onset, chronicity, certainty,   laterality) in the ``lookup_term`` field, and to emit assertion   and confidence as required fields.

designOutputs.title: Entity provenance and audit-trail surface
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-B2C85448 covering the provenance + audit-trail implementation surface. Components: libs/ner/span_resolver.py (character offsets, DI-B2512CB3), :Entity snippet_hash on document writes (tamper detection, DI-B2512CB3), services/ui review highlight renderer (DI-E81545BE), libs/ner/context_engine.py assertion evidence windows (DI-23822663), CodingReview correction event schema + services/api correction endpoints (DI-4F67189B), services/api/app/routers/audit.py + services/fhir_api/app/routers/audit_event.py audit trail APIs (DI-09E26C1D). Code-gap (tracked in improvements-backlog): append-only write-once enforcement + 7-year retention policy engine for DI-080A2454 - current retention is infra-level not application-enforced.

userNeed.title: A QA lead, knowledge author or NLP reviewer needs one place to keep test patients that check every part of the AI: reading notes, building the patient story, checking guideline rules, and writing the SBAR handover
userNeed.description: As a QA lead, knowledge author, NLP reviewer or clinical lead, I need one library that holds test patients I can use to check every part of the AI before a change goes live. The four parts I care about are: the AI tool that reads clinical notes and pulls out clinical codes; the AI tool that builds the patient story across encounters; the rule checker that flags safety issues against guidelines; and the AI tool that writes the SBAR handover. I want the test patients to look as close to real patients as possible. Where it helps, I want to copy a real patient, remove their identifying details, and save the result as a test patient.

designInputs.title: The Test Patients page shall live in the Knowledge area of the admin app, with a filter for which part of the AI to test
designInputs.description: The system SHALL show the test patient library as a tab called Test Patients inside /admin/knowledge, next to the existing tabs (Training Data, Surface Forms, Context Rules, AI Instructions, Clinical Guidelines, Pathways, Domains, Terminology, AI Summarisation). The page SHALL show four count tiles at the top, one for each part of the AI, showing how many test patients are saved, passing and regressing. A filter at the top of the table SHALL let the reviewer choose All or one of the four parts of the AI. There SHALL be one main button called Build patient whose form changes depending on which part of the AI is selected. Each row SHALL have an Edit button and a Replay button. The old page at /admin/guidance/test-patients SHALL be removed and every link to it inside the codebase SHALL be updated.

designInputs.title: The system shall keep test patients in the same shape as real patients, with a clear test marker, so the AI tools read them the same way
designInputs.description: The system SHALL store every test patient in the patient database with the same structure as a real patient (encounters, documents, observations, values, units, clinical codes, pathway state). Every test patient SHALL be marked clearly as a test record by carrying a separate test patient label and an is_test = true flag. Every test patient SHALL also carry a tag saying which part of the AI it is for: reading notes, building the patient story, checking guideline rules, or writing the SBAR handover. The system SHALL offer a copy-a-real-patient-and-de-identify action that takes a real patient, copies the structure under a new test record, removes all identifying details (NHS number, name, date of birth, address, phone numbers), and puts test_ in front of the display name. Lists, dashboards and exports that show real patients SHALL never include test patients.

verificationTests.title: Centralised test patient library: data shape, cross-graph copy, redaction, SBAR seed, dialog wiring, per-aspect editor, AI authoring AND SBAR / referral triage surfacing (relabel + outcome filter + NG12 backfill)
verificationTests.description: Hermetic verification of the test patient library across Phase A (data shape + cross-graph copy + SBAR seed + dialog wiring), Phase B (per-aspect editor), the two AI-assisted authoring flows (flow 1 scaffold-from-rule, flow 2 author-from-scenario), and the SBAR / referral triage surfacing work (relabel the 'summarisation' aspect to 'SBAR / referral triage' to make NG12 referral triage scope explicit; add a triage-outcome chip filter visible only on the SBAR aspect that shows counts per outcome (2ww, urgent, routine, no rule fired, evaluator outage, unset) and lets the reviewer narrow the table; backfill the SBAR golden set with 7 NG12 suspected-cancer pathways (bladder, endometrial, melanoma, pancreatic, head and neck, prostate, sarcoma) plus 2 adversarial 'red flag word but criteria not met' cases (haematuria with active UTI in patient under 45; pigmented lesion with 7-point checklist score 1) so the rule engine is held to NG12 coverage AND to the negative cases that reject premature 2WW escalation). New fixtures whose rules are not yet seeded in the rule engine are explicitly marked draft: true so the runner skips structural assertions on them and counts them as drafts in the run summary -- this keeps the test honest (no silent failures) without blocking the backfill on parallel rule-engine work.

userNeed.title: Infer cancer or benign pathway outcome from post-specialist encounter signals
userNeed.description: Quality leads and clinicians reviewing stale_post_specialist episodes need the system to scan the 180 days of encounters following a specialist visit and determine, from textual signals alone, whether the outcome was likely cancer (requiring further action) or benign (pathway complete). Where a clear inference can be made it should be stored with a confidence score and earliest inferred date so that time-to-outcome milestones can be calculated even when no formal SNOMED diagnosis was coded. Where no inference is possible the episode must be flagged for human review.

designInputs.title: Post-specialist outcome inference engine for stale episodes
designInputs.description: The system SHALL implement a post-specialist outcome inference engine that, for every stale_post_specialist EpisodeOfCare node, scans encounters in the 180-day window following the specialist_visit_date for textual signals that indicate a cancer or benign outcome, and writes the inferred_outcome, inferred_outcome_date (date of the earliest signal-firing encounter), inferred_confidence (0.0-0.95), and inference_signals (pipe-separated labels) onto the episode node. Where no signals are present the episode SHALL remain with inferred_outcome null and hitl_flag true.

designOutputs.title: Post-specialist outcome inference engine and analytics integration
designOutputs.description: Implements a third pass in the episode builder pipeline that scans post-specialist encounters for textual outcome signals and writes inferred_outcome, inferred_outcome_date, inferred_confidence, and inference_signals onto stale_post_specialist EpisodeOfCare nodes. Integrates the inferred outcome date into analytics KPI and audit Cypher queries as a fallback for the diagnostic interval. Exposes all four new fields via the episode_timeline API endpoint and renders amber confidence badges in the dashboard and audit UX.

userNeed.title: Clinical audit teams need patient records automatically shortlisted for programme relevance
userNeed.description: As a clinical coder or audit programme manager, I need the system to automatically retrieve and rank patient encounters from FHIR records by relevance to the configured audit programme, so that my review effort is focused on clinically relevant encounters rather than manually filtering thousands of records.

designInputs.title: Programme inclusion criteria stored as versioned configuration applied without code deployment
designInputs.description: The system SHALL store patient inclusion criteria for each audit programme as versioned configuration data, applied consistently at each pipeline run without requiring code changes, with full version history retained.

designInputs.title: Multi-mode encounter shortlisting: keyword, full-text, and vector similarity search with configurable fusion
designInputs.description: The system SHALL apply keyword matching, BM25 full-text search, and vector similarity search in parallel across programme-defined clinical domains when shortlisting patient encounters for audit review, with modality fusion weights configurable per programme.

designInputs.title: PromptConfig with smart few-shot selection and prompt caching
designInputs.description: The system SHALL provide PromptConfig controls for smart few-shot selection and prompt caching, including a configurable maximum few-shot count, a per-example core flag, and provider-aware runtime selection of relevant examples while preserving de-identification and auditability.

designInputs.title: End-to-end single-patient pipeline processing within 10 seconds at the 95th percentile
designInputs.description: The system SHALL complete the full pipeline processing cycle for a single patient — including FHIR record retrieval, NLP entity extraction, guideline evaluation, episode construction, and quality validation — within 10 seconds at the 95th percentile under normal operating conditions.

designInputs.title: Shortlisting recall quality gate: minimum 95% recall on gold-standard labelled dataset
designInputs.description: The system SHALL measure shortlisting recall against a gold-standard labelled dataset at each model release and SHALL enforce a minimum recall quality gate of 0.95 that blocks production promotion of any shortlisting model that fails this threshold.

designInputs.title: Ranked patient shortlist with fused relevance score and supporting evidence spans
designInputs.description: The system SHALL return patient shortlists as ranked results with a fused relevance score, supporting evidence spans, and programme coverage estimate for each candidate, displayed to the reviewer on the shortlisting results screen.

designInputs.title: Lab-value guard prevents diagnostic inference from observable measurements
designInputs.description: The coding pipeline SHALL NOT infer a clinical diagnosis from a lab result value. Lab measurements (e.g. eGFR, HbA1c, creatinine, sodium, haemoglobin, cholesterol, TSH, troponin, PSA, LDH, amylase, lipase, procalcitonin, NT-proBNP, CK/CPK, lactate, AFP, CA-125, CEA) SHALL be coded only as observable entities with their numeric value and unit. A disorder entity SHALL only be generated when the encounter text explicitly states a diagnosis. The lab-value guard SHALL operate on a per-entity sentence window (not the full encounter text) to avoid false suppression of legitimate diagnoses in other parts of the encounter.

designInputs.title: FHIR R4 compliant API for all patient record ingestion and audit result export
designInputs.description: The system SHALL retrieve all patient clinical records exclusively via a FHIR R4 compliant API, and SHALL export audit results and pipeline outputs as FHIR resources, so that all patient data exchange uses a standards-based interface that does not depend on proprietary source system integrations.

designOutputs.title: FHIR R4 API Service
designOutputs.description: A set of FastAPI routers that expose FHIR R4-compliant endpoints for Measure, MeasureReport, Library, and Device resources. These endpoints allow external audit programme systems to discover available quality measures, submit measure reports, and retrieve supporting library and device metadata. A dedicated Cypher generator translates FHIR search parameters into Neo4j queries so the graph database can serve as the backing store.

designOutputs.title: NER + SNOMED coding surface with assertion handling
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-0374FE26 SNOMED coding core. Components: libs/ner NER pipeline (DI-1795254D, DI-4247C7E5), libs/pipeline_graph/subgraphs SNOMED linker and assertion layer (DI-31126C6C, DI-375C7EB1), libs/pipeline/post_processing.py 9-layer post-processing, services/coding_worker runtime pipeline. Code-gap flagged in improvements-backlog: gold F1 evaluator for DI-12015DBC and per-semantic-tag threshold drift monitoring for DI-88C8BBCD.

designOutputs.title: Patient shortlisting and recall surface
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-B70ACD96 patient shortlisting. Components: services/analytics_api shortlisting service (DI-143F69EB, DI-4746A178), recall evaluation (DI-10BB41E9), shortlist export + audit (DI-1501326A).

designOutputs.title: Smart Few-Shot Selection + Prompt Caching
designOutputs.description: Runtime prompt assembly enhancement with static core examples, dynamic few-shot retrieval by similarity, and Bedrock cache-point marking. Includes PromptConfig schema/API/UI support for maxFewShot and core flags persisted in Neo4j.

designOutputs.title: Terminology API Service
designOutputs.description: Provides REST endpoints for SNOMED CT and dm+d terminology operations including free-text search, concept resolution, value set expansion, concept map translation, and clinician-initiated writeback of coding corrections. The service reads from the terminology Neo4j instance and writes corrections back through a controlled writeback pipeline that records provenance and triggers re-evaluation of affected records.

designOutputs.title: NLP training, audit agent, and FHIR exposure surface
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for active learning + model improvement cycle, audit agent with bounded auto-fix, benchmark charts in audit exports, FHIR R4 downstream exposure, pathway interval calculations, episode validation, and end-to-end single-patient pipeline SLA. UNs: UN-5236129E, UN-1AC15812, UN-299200A0, UN-94833CA3, UN-5C67AAD9, UN-2C01CF40. Components: libs/training, libs/audit_agent, services/fhir_api, services/coding_worker pipeline.

designOutputs.title: Container Infrastructure
designOutputs.description: Azure Container Apps infrastructure defined as Bicep templates with supporting Dockerfiles for each service. The Bicep modules provision the container environment, Key Vault for secrets, and configure auto-scaling rules. Dockerfiles produce minimal, reproducible images for each ACA service; coding and analysis logic ships inside the pipeline-worker image via shared Python packages (no separate worker images).

designInputs.title: DI-LEO-AI-527: Similar-candidates batch dialog highlighter + match rationale chips
designInputs.description: The 'Apply to similar candidates' batch dialog (services/ui/src/components/gold-dataset/SimilarCandidatesBatch.tsx) SHALL render shared <HighlightedText> titles and an outlined match-rationale chip row using the same encounterRelevance vocabulary as DI-LEO-AI-520 / DI-LEO-AI-523, so the last 'encounter list with a search box' surface speaks the same vocabulary as /care/encounters, the /care/patients drawer, and the dry-run review queue. SimilarCandidatesBatch SHALL accept a search?: string prop forwarded by GoldDatasetPanel.tsx (the panel's debouncedSearch), expand it once per render via useMemo(() => expandSearchTerms(search)), per-row compute matchRationale = computeMatchRationale(item.text, expandedTerms) and highlightTerms = collectHighlightTerms(search, hitTerms), conditionally wrap the truncated row text in <HighlightedText testId='similar-candidate-row-highlight'>, and render a Box (data-testid 'similar-candidate-row-match-rationale') of up to 4 outlined Chips (data-testid 'similar-candidate-row-match-rationale-chip', variant='outlined', height 20, fontSize 0.65rem). The change MUST be additive: blank queries / no expansion / no hits all fall back to the prior plain text with no behavioural change. Reuses pure-TS mission-control/encounterRelevance.ts and mission-control/HighlightedText.tsx unchanged (UN-LEO-AI-096).

designInputs.title: DI-LEO-AI-526: Server-side search term expansion for the dry-run review queue
designInputs.description: The /admin/training Candidates and Gold-label review-queue endpoints (GET /api/training/candidates and GET /api/training/gold-labels) SHALL expand the reviewer's free-text search query using the same deterministic typo and synonym vocabulary as the host encounter search on /care/encounters before the cypher filter is applied, so a query for 'lump' surfaces TrainingCandidate / GoldLabel rows that wrote 'mass', 'swelling', or 'nodule' in the same single page. A new pure-Python helper libs/search/term_expansion.py SHALL hold the single source of truth for the typo correction map (TYPO_MAP), synonym map (SYNONYM_MAP), and an expand_search_terms(query) function. The analytics-layer encounter_query_understanding.py SHALL be refactored to import the same maps and helper from this module. GET_TRAINING_CANDIDATES_PAGE / COUNT_TRAINING_CANDIDATES_PAGE / GET_GOLD_LABELS_PAGE / COUNT_GOLD_LABELS_PAGE SHALL accept an optional $terms parameter (lower-case array). When non-empty, the cypher OR-matches via ANY(t IN $terms WHERE toLower(c.text) CONTAINS t); when empty/NULL, falls back to the legacy $search substring filter via CASE for backward compatibility. The training router and neo4j_mcp tools SHALL forward the expanded terms to both page and count queries on the same request. Mirrors DI-LEO-AI-520 and DI-LEO-AI-523 (UN-LEO-AI-096).

designOutputs.title: Holdout Set Selection Script and Export Contamination Guard

Post-training evaluation stores results as DriftMetric with metric_type='training_eval'.

designOutputs.title: NER Training Export Script with PII Gate, Stratification Report, and Safety Block
designOutputs.description: Implements export_ner_training.py: queries confirmed/reviewed DOCUMENTS relationships excluding holdout and sentinel records, groups by encounter and sentence, strips all patient-linkable identifiers, runs detect_phi() on every evidence_sentence (abort on detection), outputs ner_training_gold.jsonl, ner_training_silver.jsonl, ner_stratification_report.txt, ner_export_manifest.json. Otherwise existing diagnosis-led and stale-close behaviour is unchanged.

designOutputs.title: Unified Encounter Coding Agent
designOutputs.description: A LangGraph StateGraph implementing a clinical coding/audit agent with SNOMED terminology tools. Three nodes:   load_encounter  -- formats state, sets mode/tier/token budget   coder           -- cyclic LLM + tool dispatch loop   post_process    -- validates verdict, adds metadata, extracts NER offsets  Seven Bedrock toolSpec tools are provided: search_snomed, lookup_concept, resolve_evidence, get_patient_demographics, get_patient_problems, read_context, submit_verdict (terminal). The graph loops between coder and the tool dispatch inside coder until submit_verdict is called, max iterations is hit, or the token budget is exhausted. The post_process node adds the metadata block and validates character offsets.  In audit mode the verdict matches the legacy format (missing, overcoded, wrong_assertion) for backward compatibility with the audit pipeline. In code mode the verdict contains an entities list with action=add for all extracted concepts. Both modes include sentence+offset for NER data.

userNeed.title: NLP engineers need the NER model to classify the same text span under multiple SNOMED semantic types simultaneously
userNeed.description: As an NLP engineer building a clinical entity recognition model, I need the NER pipeline to support classification of the same text span under multiple SNOMED semantic types simultaneously, so that a clinical entity that is both a disorder and a finding — or both a procedure and an observable — is correctly represented without forcing a single label that loses clinical meaning.

designInputs.title: Label verification step multi-label annotation fidelity
designInputs.description: The system SHALL ensure that the label verification step reads, displays, and writes back all SNOMED type labels for every span-label pair in a multi-label annotation without collapsing or dropping any label; any reduction in the label count between input and output is treated as a pipeline failure.

designInputs.title: Multi-type span classification for overlapping SNOMED concepts
designInputs.description: The NER pipeline SHALL emit zero or more SNOMED concept assignments per text span when clinically valid, preserving all non-conflicting semantic types rather than forcing a single winner-take-all label.

designInputs.title: LLM semantic tag scope constraint to validated NER model output set
designInputs.description: The system SHALL enforce that the LLM extraction step cannot introduce SNOMED semantic type labels that were not produced by the NER model for the same document; any additional semantic tags SHALL be detected and removed by the post-processing layer before the result is stored or returned.

designInputs.title: Post-processing preservation of overlapping same-label spans with divergent terminology lookups
designInputs.description: The system SHALL preserve overlapping spans that share the same SNOMED semantic type label when their normalised terminology lookup terms differ, treating them as distinct clinical entities rather than duplicates requiring deduplication.

designInputs.title: Inference API response schema: one result per span-label pair for multi-type spans
designInputs.description: The system SHALL define and enforce an inference API response schema that returns one entity object per span-label pair, enabling downstream consumers to receive multiple typed results for the same character span without requiring additional queries.

designInputs.title: Lossless multi-label span export to model training format
designInputs.description: The system SHALL export gold label records containing multi-label spans as one training record per span-label pair, preserving character offsets, entity text, and label independently for each type assignment, so that no label is lost during the transition from annotation to model training.

designOutputs.title: Label-verification and training-export lossless writer
designOutputs.description:
Retrospective DO documenting `services/api/app/services/label_verifier.py::_process_label` and `libs/ner/training_label_writer.py` which together process and export one record per span-label pair through the label-verification queue to the training JSONL export.

Gap (tracked in improvements-backlog batch-04 / DI-EE80C271 + DI-6EFD68D0): no count-in == count-out invariant is currently enforced so silent collapse of multi-label span pairs would not be detected by existing tests.

designOutputs.title: Multi-label NER schema mapper and post-processing normalisation
designOutputs.description:
Retrospective DO documenting `libs/ner/schema_mapper.py` (VALID_RELATION_TYPES, stable entity-id hashing that keys on (doc_id, start, end, label) so same-span differing-label entities are both retained) and `libs/pipeline/post_processing.py` normalisation, which together give the runtime + training paths one entity per span-label pair.

Gap (tracked in improvements-backlog batch-04): dedupe does not branch on lookup_term when two same-(start,end,label) entries differ on clinical qualifier; and LLM scope guard does not enforce per-document subset against NER label set.

designOutputs.title: Multi-label NER - spancat component, layer 5 nesting refinement, prompt preservation
designOutputs.description: Eight coordinated changes to support multi-label span classification:  1. base.cfg: pipeline switched from ["transformer","ner"] to    ["transformer","spancat"]. NER component block replaced with    SpanCategorizer.v1 using ngram_range_suggester (min_size=1,    max_size=10) and TransformerListener. Score weights updated to    spans_sc_f. Suggester upgraded from ngram_suggester sizes=[1..5]    to ngram_range_suggester max_size=10 to cover entity spans up to    10 tokens (p95 of gold-label corpus), recovering 11.6% of training    spans that were silently dropped by the 5-token cap.  2. label_exporter._record_to_spacy_doc(): seen_tokens dedup guard    removed. doc.ents assignment replaced with doc.spans["sc"] so    overlapping and co-located spans are all written to DocBin.  3. evaluator._build_per_label(): reads spans_sc_per_type instead    of ents_per_type. Score threshold checks updated to spans_sc_f.  4. model_inference /extract: iterates doc.spans.get("sc", []) for    post-spancat models; falls back to doc.ents with a logged warning    for pre-spancat model artifacts (backward compatibility).  5. post_processing.normalise_entity_types(): same-label nesting    suppression now only fires when both spans share an identical    normalized lookup term. Spans with the same label but different    normalized terms are both preserved.  6. extraction_v1.py: SEMANTIC TAG RULES section updated to clarify    "one semantic_tag per output entry; do not emit multiple entries    for the same

userNeed.title: Clinical NLP pipeline must completely capture test result values for observable entities
userNeed.description: The post-processing pipeline attaches numeric values (e.g. 7.2 mmol/L) to observable entities during Layer 6 value-unit linking. However, two common clinical patterns are not captured: 1) String-based results - A test result expressed as positive, negative, or borderline is reclassified as a qualifier_value entity but is never formally linked to its parent observable entity. Downstream analytics cannot query eGFR result = negative without this link. 2) Value before entity - When a numeric or string result appears before the observable name in the encounter text (e.g. 7.2 mmol/L HbA1c or negative -- Urine culture), no value is attached because the pipeline relies only on extracted measurement entities and does not scan the raw text window preceding the observable. Both gaps mean that observable entities leave the pipeline with obs.value = None even when a result is clearly present in the encounter text, degrading the quality of clinical data extracted for audit and pathway analysis.

designInputs.title: Layer 6 value-unit linker extension for string descriptors and raw-text fallback
designInputs.description: The post-processing Layer 6 value-unit linker SHALL be extended to: (1) attach string-based result descriptors (positive, negative, borderline, reactive, non-reactive, and all other terms in _RESULT_DESCRIPTOR_TEXTS) as obs[value] on the nearest observable_entity within 40 characters; (2) perform a raw-text window scan of up to 60 characters preceding an observable entity's start offset to capture numeric or string values that were not extracted as separate entity spans by the NER model; and (3) accept an optional encounter_text parameter so that both the entity-list path and the raw-text fallback path operate in a single function call without breaking existing callers.

designOutputs.title: Extended value-unit linker in post-processing Layer 6
designOutputs.description: Extends link_observable_value_units in libs/pipeline/post_processing.py with two additional linking passes beyond the existing numeric entity pass:  Pass 2 - String result linking:   Builds a list of entity indices whose text is in _RESULT_DESCRIPTOR_TEXTS.   For each observable_entity that still has no value, finds the nearest   string result entity within 40 characters and sets obs["value"] to the   lowercased text and obs["unit"] to "".  Pass 3 - Raw-text fallback scan:   When encounter_text is provided, scans a window of up to 60 characters   immediately before each still-unlinked observable entity's start offset.   Applies _VALUE_UNIT_RE for numeric matches and _RESULT_DESCRIPTOR_TEXTS   for string matches. Attaches the last (closest) match found.  The function signature gains an optional encounter_text: str = "" parameter. The call site in run_post_processing threads the existing encounter_text argument through.  A new private predicate _is_string_result_text is added alongside _is_numeric_measurement_text for use in Pass 2.

designOutputs.title: Episode builder fallback referral-claim and evidence-wins merge
designOutputs.description: Two correlated updates to the episode-builder package:  1. Two-pass referral matching: strict same-site Pass 1 followed    by site-agnostic Pass 2 for diagnoses that remain floating.    ep.referral_match_method tags every episode with    'strict_site' | 'fallback_any_site' | 'none'. When Pass 2    still leaves a diagnosis floating, ep.referral_date is    NULL (never back-filled from the diagnosis date) and    ep.referral_inferred is false.  2. Evidence-wins duplicate merging: per-patient referral-date    clustering (including NSS episodes), text corroboration of    cancer_type against the diagnosis_confirmed encounter text,    and a new MOVE_LINKS_Q Cypher query that migrates every    IS_PART_OF edge from duplicates to the primary, preserving    milestone_type.  Together these changes bring the canonical confirmed-cancer count in line with the true patient cohort and raise the 2WW-route subset to reflect UK primary-care reality.

userNeed.title: Junior clinical and coding staff can complete audit, coding review, and pathway tasks on LEO without prior product training
userNeed.description: A large share of real LEO users are new staff: medical students, F1/F2 doctors, practice nurses in their first year, trainee coders, and apprentices. Their needs are different from experienced clinicians. They are efficient if the product explains why they are here, what each thing does, and what will happen next. They are unsafe if the product assumes mastery. Existing user needs assume a clinical audit lead or coding specialist persona. There is no explicit design input anywhere requiring explanation patterns, onboarding tours, or progressive reveal. This UN creates that requirement.

designInputs.title: Care Overview PageIntro and accessible summary card typography
designInputs.description: The Care Overview page (services/ui/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx) SHALL render the shared PageIntro primitive as the first block below the date filter so that, on first load, a junior staff member or older clinician sees a plain-language explanation of why they are on this page, how to read the four summary cards and two chart rows, and what the date filter changes. The chart section titles and their supporting descriptions SHALL meet Flesch-Kincaid Grade level 9 or below. The four summary StatCard values SHALL remain single-number focal points with larger (>=2rem) numerals and plain-language captions; uppercase chip-style labels on summary cards SHALL be softened to sentence case with 12px minimum font size.

designInputs.title: Motion layer with framer-motion and prefers-reduced-motion gating
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single motion layer built on framer-motion, with pre-canned transitions (default 180 ms ease-out, 220 ms spring for route change, 120 ms for hover and focus). All motion SHALL be gated by the browser's prefers-reduced-motion media query so users who have requested reduced motion receive an instant state change with no animation.

designInputs.title: Five reusable explanation primitives (PageIntro, HelpPopover, CoachMark, ProgressiveReveal, GlossaryTerm)
designInputs.description: The LEO UI SHALL expose five reusable explanation primitives (PageIntro, HelpPopover, CoachMark, ProgressiveReveal, GlossaryTerm) that every screen consumes to answer, for the current persona, (a) Why am I here, (b) How do I do the task, (c) What will happen next. GlossaryTerm MUST read its definition from a single source-of-truth glossary keyed by clinical term. All patient-reachable copy rendered through these primitives MUST be written at Flesch-Kincaid Grade level 9 or below.

designInputs.title: Coding-review bulk modal split with plain-language explanations
designInputs.description: The coding-review bulk case modal SHALL be split into multiple modules, each no longer than 500 lines of code, and SHALL expose plain-language explanations via the shared PageIntro, GlossaryTerm, and HelpPopover primitives so that a junior trainee can understand, for any given case, why it needs review, what each SNOMED term means in everyday words, and what will happen when they accept, code differently, or suppress.

designInputs.title: Single @leo/design-system workspace package for tokens, primitives, motion, copy
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single design-system workspace package (@leo/design-system) that owns tokens (colour, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, density), primitives (shell, role gate, knowledge page, stat hero, progressive reveal, task queue), motion infra, and role-scoped copy. All UI services SHALL import from this package; no service SHALL ship duplicated local copies of these concerns.

designInputs.title: DM Sans typography via next/font with humanist sans for clinical labels
designInputs.description: The system SHALL load DM Sans via next/font/google (preload, subset, self-hosted) and use it for all body, heading, and subtitle typography. Monospace (JetBrains Mono) SHALL be reserved for <code>, <kbd>, and raw SNOMED identifiers; subtitle1 and subtitle2 variants SHALL switch from mono to DM Sans 600.

designOutputs.title: services/design-system as npm workspace package '@leo/design-system'
designOutputs.description: Introduces a root package.json declaring workspaces, a new services/design-system package, and updates services/ui to consume it via transpilePackages + a TypeScript path alias. The package owns tokens, motion, fonts, primitives, roles, and copy helpers.

designOutputs.title: Coding review modal split and plain-language redesign
designOutputs.description: This output refactors the 1123-line CodingReviewCasesModal.tsx into five modules, each at or below 500 lines, preserves the public API, and surfaces plain-language explanations via shared primitives:  - CodingReviewCasesModal.tsx -- the dialog shell, bulk   actions, label menu, and orchestration of CaseCards. - CaseCard.tsx -- per-case UI: Ask LEO, accept, code,   suppress, assertion correction. - EncounterContextPanel.tsx -- the siblings widget for   context from the same encounter. - codingReviewUtils.ts -- pure helpers (safety warning   detection, extractSuggestedPhrase, keyframes). - codingReviewCopy.ts -- all PageIntro copy and glossary   keys used on this screen.  The dialog adds a PageIntro at the top explaining why this queue exists, how to work it, and what each action does. Clinical terms (assertion, semantic tag, suppress, declined, absent, hypothetical, planned) render through GlossaryTerm or HelpPopover with FK grade <=9 copy.

designOutputs.title: PageIntro + HelpPopover + CoachMark + ProgressiveReveal + GlossaryTerm + glossary.ts + readability.ts
designOutputs.description: Five explanation primitives exported from services/ui/src/components/ui/. A glossary module in services/ui/src/lib/glossary.ts provides (label, clinicalTerm, plainLanguage) triplets keyed by termId. A readability utility computes Flesch-Kincaid Grade to gate shipped copy in CI. - PageIntro: SSR-safe, persists collapse state per   screen in localStorage. - HelpPopover: MUI Popover with role='dialog',   aria-labelledby, Escape-closes. - CoachMark: portal-rendered overlay tied to an anchor   ref; respects prefers-reduced-motion; dismissal   persists in localStorage 'leo-tour-<tour-id>-done'. - ProgressiveReveal: MUI Collapse wrapped with   aria-expanded disclosure button. - GlossaryTerm: renders an underlined span that opens a   HelpPopover with plainLanguage; tree-shakeable import.

designOutputs.title: MotionProvider, useMotion, and pre-canned transitions
designOutputs.description: Adds framer-motion as a services/ui dependency. Introduces @leo/design-system/motion exporting MotionProvider and useMotion() that returns { reducedMotion, transitions }. Transitions collapse to duration 0 when reducedMotion is true.

designOutputs.title: Mission Control Analytics API Router
designOutputs.description: FastAPI router module at services/analytics_api/app/routers/mission_control.py implementing three endpoints:  1. GET /analytics/mission-control/patients    - Builds on _audit_helpers._episode_base for org scoping and      date range filtering.    - Adds pathway_filter (confirmed|closures|all), cancer_types,      closure_reasons, and review_status query parameters.    - Returns paginated envelope: total, page, page_size, patients[].    - Each patient entry contains demographics and nested episodes[],      each episode containing: episode_id, cancer_type, status,      cancer_stage, referral_date, diagnosis_date,      diagnostic_interval_days, primary_care_interval_days,      safety_netting (bool), reviewed_by, reviewed_at, audit_flag,      audit_notes, milestones[].    - Pagination via SKIP/LIMIT Cypher; sorting via ORDER BY.  2. GET /analytics/mission-control/kpis    - Same filter params as /patients (minus pagination).    - Single aggregation Cypher returning:      total_patients, confirmed_cancer, pathway_closures,      median_diagnostic_interval_days, safety_netting_rate,      needs_review_count.  3. PATCH /analytics/mission-control/episodes/{episode_id}/review    - Writes reviewed_by, reviewed_at=datetime(), audit_notes,      audit_flag to matching EpisodeOfCare node.    - Does NOT alter any clinical coding properties.    - Requires authenticated caller (HTTP 401 if unauthenticated).
