userNeed.title: Experienced clinicians with age-related vision, hearing, or dexterity changes can use LEO at full professional speed
userNeed.description: Primary care is staffed by clinicians across the full adult age range, including partners in their 60s and 70s and returners working reduced hours. These users are highly expert but their interface needs differ from younger users: larger default text, generous target sizes, high-contrast options, no thin strokes, no low-contrast grey-on-grey, no time-pressured interactions, no animations that distract, and a keyboard-first option for every mouse gesture. They are also the product most senior reviewers and safety owners. If LEO is unpleasant or tiring for them, clinical oversight suffers. An explicit persona makes these needs testable.

designInputs.title: LEO UI design tokens and accessible theme foundation
designInputs.description: The LEO UI SHALL expose a single, typed, tokenised design system (colour pairs, type scale, spacing scale, radius scale, motion scale, focus ring) that every surface consumes through MUI theme and matching CSS custom properties. Tokens MUST guarantee a minimum 16px base body font size, a minimum 12px chip/caption size, >=4.5:1 text contrast, >=3:1 non-text contrast, a >=3px visible focus ring with >=3:1 contrast, and MUST support prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme at the CSS custom-property level so any component can adapt without duplicating logic.

designInputs.title: Care Overview PageIntro and accessible summary card typography
designInputs.description: The Care Overview page (services/ui/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx) SHALL render the shared PageIntro primitive as the first block below the date filter so that, on first load, a junior staff member or older clinician sees a plain-language explanation of why they are on this page, how to read the four summary cards and two chart rows, and what the date filter changes. The chart section titles and their supporting descriptions SHALL meet Flesch-Kincaid Grade level 9 or below. The four summary StatCard values SHALL remain single-number focal points with larger (>=2rem) numerals and plain-language captions; uppercase chip-style labels on summary cards SHALL be softened to sentence case with 12px minimum font size.

designInputs.title: LEO UI density modes (Compact, Comfortable, Spacious) with patient-route safe defaults
designInputs.description: The LEO UI SHALL expose three density modes - Compact, Comfortable (default for staff), and Spacious (default for patient-reachable routes) - controlled by a DensityProvider React context whose value is driven by a user preference persisted to the browser (localStorage key leo-density) and read at app-root. Every primitive component (Button, Chip, Input, Table row, ListItem, Card) MUST resolve its padding, min-height, and font-size from the active density tier. Patient-reachable routes under /portal, /mail, /safety-netting, /games, /care/wellbeing, and /sign-in MUST default to Spacious. Spacious MUST guarantee >=44x44 CSS pixel touch targets.

designInputs.title: Motion layer with framer-motion and prefers-reduced-motion gating
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single motion layer built on framer-motion, with pre-canned transitions (default 180 ms ease-out, 220 ms spring for route change, 120 ms for hover and focus). All motion SHALL be gated by the browser's prefers-reduced-motion media query so users who have requested reduced motion receive an instant state change with no animation.

designInputs.title: Coding-review bulk modal split with plain-language explanations
designInputs.description: The coding-review bulk case modal SHALL be split into multiple modules, each no longer than 500 lines of code, and SHALL expose plain-language explanations via the shared PageIntro, GlossaryTerm, and HelpPopover primitives so that a junior trainee can understand, for any given case, why it needs review, what each SNOMED term means in everyday words, and what will happen when they accept, code differently, or suppress.

designInputs.title: Single @leo/design-system workspace package for tokens, primitives, motion, copy
designInputs.description: The system SHALL expose a single design-system workspace package (@leo/design-system) that owns tokens (colour, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, density), primitives (shell, role gate, knowledge page, stat hero, progressive reveal, task queue), motion infra, and role-scoped copy. All UI services SHALL import from this package; no service SHALL ship duplicated local copies of these concerns.

designInputs.title: DM Sans typography via next/font with humanist sans for clinical labels
designInputs.description: The system SHALL load DM Sans via next/font/google (preload, subset, self-hosted) and use it for all body, heading, and subtitle typography. Monospace (JetBrains Mono) SHALL be reserved for <code>, <kbd>, and raw SNOMED identifiers; subtitle1 and subtitle2 variants SHALL switch from mono to DM Sans 600.

designOutputs.title: DensityProvider and density-aware primitive resolution
designOutputs.description: - DensityContext exports a React context with value   'compact' | 'comfortable' | 'spacious' and a setter. - DensityProvider decides the initial value using route-match   (patient-reachable prefixes) + localStorage + default. - useDensity() returns the current value; useDensityTokens()   returns the padding/min-height/font-size map for the   active tier from theme/tokens.ts DENSITY_MAP. - Settings page exposes a Density toggle; writes to   localStorage 'leo-density' and updates context. - Patient-reachable routes (/portal, /mail, /safety-netting,   /games, /care/wellbeing, /sign-in) force 'spacious'.

designOutputs.title: services/design-system as npm workspace package '@leo/design-system'
designOutputs.description: Introduces a root package.json declaring workspaces, a new services/design-system package, and updates services/ui to consume it via transpilePackages + a TypeScript path alias. The package owns tokens, motion, fonts, primitives, roles, and copy helpers.

designOutputs.title: Coding review modal split and plain-language redesign
designOutputs.description: This output refactors the 1123-line CodingReviewCasesModal.tsx into five modules, each at or below 500 lines, preserves the public API, and surfaces plain-language explanations via shared primitives:  - CodingReviewCasesModal.tsx -- the dialog shell, bulk   actions, label menu, and orchestration of CaseCards. - CaseCard.tsx -- per-case UI: Ask LEO, accept, code,   suppress, assertion correction. - EncounterContextPanel.tsx -- the siblings widget for   context from the same encounter. - codingReviewUtils.ts -- pure helpers (safety warning   detection, extractSuggestedPhrase, keyframes). - codingReviewCopy.ts -- all PageIntro copy and glossary   keys used on this screen.  The dialog adds a PageIntro at the top explaining why this queue exists, how to work it, and what each action does. Clinical terms (assertion, semantic tag, suppress, declined, absent, hypothetical, planned) render through GlossaryTerm or HelpPopover with FK grade <=9 copy.

designOutputs.title: Token source of truth for LEO UI: theme.ts, theme/tokens.ts, theme/tokens.css
designOutputs.description: - theme/tokens.ts exports TYPE_SCALE, SPACING, RADIUS, MOTION,   FOCUS_RING, and CONTRAST_PAIRS objects. Each pair is a   {fg, bg, role} triplet with >=4.5:1 computed contrast. - theme.ts consumes tokens.ts, adds h1..h6 typography   overrides with minimum 16px body, and enables focus-visible   outlines that meet size and contrast. - theme/tokens.css emits each token as a CSS custom property   under :root and inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion:   reduce) to zero non-essential animation duration and   inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) to swap colour   pairs. It is imported once in layout.tsx. - layout.tsx sets html.lang and html.dir; globals.css keeps   print rules, removes the hardcoded 14px from .skip-link,   adds prefers-reduced-motion overrides.

designOutputs.title: next/font DM Sans + subtitle1/2 un-monospaced
designOutputs.description: Adds @leo/design-system/fonts that exports dmSans and jetBrainsMono loaders configured via next/font/google. services/ui/src/app/layout.tsx applies dmSans.className. Theme typography updated so subtitle1 and subtitle2 use DM Sans 600 instead of JetBrains Mono.

designOutputs.title: MotionProvider, useMotion, and pre-canned transitions
designOutputs.description: Adds framer-motion as a services/ui dependency. Introduces @leo/design-system/motion exporting MotionProvider and useMotion() that returns { reducedMotion, transitions }. Transitions collapse to duration 0 when reducedMotion is true.

userNeed.title: Clinical reviewers need plain-language AI interpretation of coded audit findings
userNeed.description: As a clinical reviewer working through a coded episode or audit alert, I need the system to generate a plain-language interpretation of what the coded data shows clinically, so that I can quickly understand the significance of a finding without needing to interpret raw SNOMED codes and interval calculations myself.

designInputs.title: Plain-language interpretation of coded findings for reviewers
designInputs.description: For each reviewer-selected coded finding, the system SHALL generate a plain-English interpretation at the configured reading level with linked source codes and explicit uncertainty when evidence is partial.

designInputs.title: Diagnostic and treatment recommendation exclusion from generated interpretations
designInputs.description: The system SHALL apply a post-generation content classification check to every AI-generated interpretation that detects and blocks outputs containing diagnostic conclusions, differential diagnoses, or treatment recommendations before the output is presented to any user or API consumer.

designInputs.title: Confidence level displayed alongside each AI-generated interpretation
designInputs.description: The system SHALL include a confidence level in every generated plain-language interpretation, derived from the confidence scores of the underlying extracted entities, presented as both a numeric value and a human-readable tier label visible to the reviewer alongside the interpretation text.

designInputs.title: Human-review gate blocking publication of AI-generated interpretations without reviewer decision
designInputs.description: The system SHALL prevent any AI-generated plain-language interpretation from being published, shared, exported, or surfaced to a downstream consumer unless a qualified reviewer has recorded an explicit accept or reject decision against that specific interpretation; the gate SHALL be enforced at the API layer, not only in the UI.

designInputs.title: Clinical significance framing: interpretation content bounded to structured input facts
designInputs.description: The system SHALL verify that every generated interpretation contains only clinical statements that are directly supported by the structured coded findings passed as input, and SHALL reject any interpretation that introduces clinical facts not present in the structured input set.

designOutputs.title: Appointment Header Filter and Resolver Input Normalisation
designOutputs.description: Two complementary precision improvements to the clinical coding pipeline:  1. Appointment/admin header filter (DI-LEO-AI-080):    is_header_sentence(text) detects administrative header lines using    a conservative regex and filter_header_sentences(chunks) removes    them from the sentence list before any extractor is called.  2. Resolver input normalisation (DI-LEO-AI-004 bug fix):    _normalise_for_resolve(text) strips trailing numeric lab values    plus SI units (e.g. "1.05 mmol/L") and EMIS local code suffixes    (e.g. "(X78gA)") from evidence phrases before they are sent to    /terminology/resolve, preventing the resolver from returning unit    qualifier concepts instead of the intended lab test concepts.

designOutputs.title: LLM Interpretation Module
designOutputs.description: Provides LLM-assisted clinical interpretation that translates structured audit and coding data into plain-language summaries readable by non-specialist users. A prompt registry manages versioned system prompts, and a factory abstracts the underlying LLM provider so the system can switch between Azure OpenAI models without code changes.

designOutputs.title: Plain-language interpretation and human-review gate
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-575E8DCB plain-language interpretation. Components: libs/prompts/interpretation_v1.py and libs/llm_client interpretation pipeline (DI-66F1B177, DI-604767B1), services/api/app/services interpretation formatter (DI-A3107424), services/ui interpretation viewer (DI-DA7584D8), reviewer sign-off gate before publish (DI-69C29EEF).

designOutputs.title: LLM-Based AppropriatenessRule Authoring with HITL Review Queue
designOutputs.description: Two-file implementation: GuidanceRuleGenerator uses the existing run_consensus() dual-model pipeline to generate AppropriatenessRule candidates from Recommendation nodes, SNOMED-codes each criterion via the terminology API, and writes draft rules (status: pending_review) to Neo4j with associated HITL ReviewTask nodes. FastAPI router exposes fire-and-track generation, list/detail/ decision review endpoints. All LLM call sites comply with llm-security.mdc.

designOutputs.title: Editable rule review dialog with versioned write-back
designOutputs.description: Two-column centred MUI Dialog (~1100 px) for editing pending AppropriatenessRule logic before approval. Reviewers can replace, add, or remove SNOMED concepts, change AT_LEAST minimums, edit demographic checks, and switch group kinds (AND / OR / NOT / AT_LEAST). The right column hosts a debounced /api/terminology/search panel bound to the focused chip or "Add concept" target.  Saving sends action="edit" with an updates payload to the existing decision endpoint. The new apply_rule_edit service validates the tree (depth, node count, structural rules, SNOMED concept existence), writes a brand-new :AppropriatenessRule node with status='active', links it to the same Recommendation, supersedes the predecessor via [:SUPERSEDES], and writes an immutable GuidanceAuditEvent.  Removed surfaces (per DI-LEO-AI-154): duplicated NICE recommendation block inside the edit surface (replaced with collapsible "View NICE source" link), and the redundant plain-English summary in the session-approved card (the recommendation_text is now shown directly).

designOutputs.title: Benign Cancer Pathway Closure Detection
designOutputs.description: The episode builder detects 'No evidence of cancer found' (SNOMED 395100000) encounters scoped to each individual episode window and closes episodes as 'closed_benign' when the concept is coded within 365 days of the referral date. A confirmed cancer diagnosis always takes precedence.  The detection is implemented as _benign_closure_for_episode() in episode_builder.py, which queries Neo4j with explicit after_date and before_date parameters derived from the referral date + 365 days. The no_cancer_discharge FHIR ValueSet is seeded into Neo4j by _seed_no_cancer_discharge_valueset.py and linked to the cancer_audit AuditDomain. Surface form aliases for benign discharge phrases and 2WW clinic shorthand are pinned via _pin_2ww_clinic_aliases.py.

userNeed.title: Pathway coordinators need pathway intervals automatically calculated against programme waiting time targets
userNeed.description: As a pathway coordinator or clinical lead, I need pathway intervals and duration metrics automatically calculated against programme-defined waiting time targets, so that I can identify breaches and delays across a patient population without manually performing date arithmetic across multiple records.

designInputs.title: Multi-level pathway metrics aggregation at organisation, PCN, and ICB with ODS-sourced hierarchy
designInputs.description: The system SHALL aggregate pathway interval metrics and breach rates at organisation (ODS), PCN, and ICB levels using a configurable hierarchy sourced from ODS reference data, with RBAC-controlled access to each aggregation tier.

designInputs.title: End-to-end single-patient pipeline processing within 10 seconds at the 95th percentile
designInputs.description: The system SHALL complete the full pipeline processing cycle for a single patient — including FHIR record retrieval, NLP entity extraction, guideline evaluation, episode construction, and quality validation — within 10 seconds at the 95th percentile under normal operating conditions.

designInputs.title: Configurable pathway interval calculation and waiting time target breach detection
designInputs.description: The system SHALL automatically calculate pathway interval values for all configured milestone pairs in each episode and SHALL assess each interval against the programme-defined target, flagging breaches with the specific interval, threshold, and overage; all definitions SHALL be stored as runtime-configurable programme data.

designInputs.title: HITL gate: pathway interval calculations use only reviewer-accepted milestone data
designInputs.description: The system SHALL ensure all pathway interval calculations and breach assessments are performed exclusively on milestone data that has been accepted by a qualified reviewer, and SHALL return a pending status rather than provisional metrics for episodes with any unreviewed milestones.

designOutputs.title: Shared libs/metrics module for NCDA interval KPIs
designOutputs.description: Extracts the NCDA interval KPI math (days_presentation_to_referral, days_referral_to_diagnosis, days_diagnosis_to_treatment) into a pure-math module at libs/metrics/ with zero Neo4j or LLM dependencies. The runtime kpi_calculator and the one-shot scripts/build_ncda_export.py both import days_between, pick_earliest_milestone, and compute_interval_kpis from this module so they produce identical numbers. The Neo4j I/O (milestone fetch, consultations-before-referral count, persistence) remains in the analyzer.

userNeed.title: Clinical informaticians need a guided research workspace to investigate populations and analyse pathway bottlenecks without data science skills
userNeed.description: As a clinical informatician, audit team lead, or pathway coordinator, I need a guided research workspace where I can investigate patient populations, discover cohorts, and analyse pathway bottlenecks by selecting from plain-English mission cards and answering a small number of scoping questions, so that I can conduct meaningful population-level analysis without needing data science skills or knowledge of the underlying graph algorithms.

designInputs.title: Research workspace results data coverage indicator with low-coverage advisory
designInputs.description: The system SHALL include a data coverage indicator on every research workspace result showing population completeness, with a prominent advisory note when coverage falls below 60%.

designInputs.title: Persona lens control reframing workspace language for different user roles without changing analysis
designInputs.description: The system SHALL provide a persona lens control on the research workspace that reframes mission titles, scoping questions, and result language for different user roles without altering the underlying analysis or data.

designInputs.title: Research workspace single-action structured export with method metadata and no patient identifiers
designInputs.description: The system SHALL provide a single-action structured file export from the research workspace results panel, including result data, scoping parameters, analysis method identifier, and coverage indicator, with no patient identifiers in the export.

designInputs.title: Guided population research workspace with plain-English scoping
designInputs.description: The research workspace SHALL guide users through mission selection and scoped questions, then run only approved graph analytics templates and return plain-English summaries with query provenance.

designOutputs.title: Encounter-centric Mission Control and Batch Reset/Recode
designOutputs.description: Implements the encounter-first Mission Control route, org-wide hybrid retrieval endpoints, and batch remediation endpoint. - UI route /care/encounters replaces /care/pathways behavior. - Analytics API provides /mission-control/encounters and /kpis. - Search supports optional near-duplicate suppression for very similar encounter text. - Search supports configurable relevance floors (combined score, vector score, keyword anchor). - Core API provides /patients/encounters/batch-reset-and-recode. - Queue payloads use pd-gp-encounter-coding with mode extract_encounter. - trigger_analysis defaults false, with explicit opt-in. - UI supports queueing all matching search results by paging and submitting chunked batches.

designOutputs.title: Pathway Explorer UI components
designOutputs.description: Implements the frontend for the Pathway Explorer research workspace. All components use MUI with sx prop and theme tokens; no hardcoded colours, no emojis, no algorithm names in user-facing text.  Components: - PathwayExplorerWorkspace.tsx -- Top-level layout with header, persona   lens toggle, split panel (card grid + results), and scoping wizard dialog - MissionCardGrid.tsx -- Groups mission cards by intent; handles loading,   error, and empty states - MissionCard.tsx -- Single card with icon, tier badge, title, description,   locked/data-gated state, keyboard navigation - PersonaLensToggle.tsx -- Segmented control for Patients/Pathways/Capacity   lens switching - ScopingWizard.tsx -- Three-question scoping dialog (area, period, detail)   with pill-button ToggleButtonGroup selectors - ResultsPanel.tsx -- Four-layer result container with tabs (Data / Method) - HeadlineResult.tsx -- Plain-English headline with coverage badge;   loading/error/unavailable states; role=status aria-live=polite - ResultsTable.tsx -- Sortable, exportable results table with plain-English   column headers - MethodExplainer.tsx -- Collapsible How did we work this out? section - GuidedNextSteps.tsx -- Contextual next mission links - useResearchState.ts -- Custom hook managing mission selection, scoping,   API polling, and result caching - researchApi.ts -- TypeScript API client for research endpoints

designOutputs.title: Research workspace and cohort builder surface
designOutputs.description: Umbrella DO for UN-47B82B96 research workspace. Components: services/analytics_api/app/services cohort builder (DI-DD67ACFF, DI-93162C3C), services/ui research workspace view (DI-9DCBC4BA), de-identification export pipeline (DI-58988BF2). Code-gap: full cohort builder UI planned but incomplete.

designOutputs.title: Pathway Explorer research API and GDS services
designOutputs.description: Implements the backend for the Pathway Explorer research workspace. Consists of four modules:  1. gds_projection_manager.py -- Creates, caches, and drops four named GDS    in-memory projections (patient-condition, condition-cooccur,    patient-journey, referral-network) with org-scoped Cypher projections    and a data-gate check for the referral-network Layer B projection.  2. algorithm_runner.py -- Maps mission IDs to GDS algorithm calls. Handles    Leiden (groups), KNN (similar), PageRank (critical), Betweenness    (bridges), Degree (busiest), Shortest Path / temporal (bottleneck), WCC    (gaps), SCC (circles), Triangle Count (teams), Adamic-Adar (missing).    Returns AlgorithmResult dataclass with headline, items, coverage info,    method text, and guided next steps.  3. headline_generator.py -- Plain-English headline templates and method    text (plain + technical) for each mission. Complies with health literacy    rules (Flesch-Kincaid Grade <= 6).  4. research.py router -- FastAPI router exposing projection management and    mission execution endpoints. Inline missions return 200; async missions    return 202 with run_id.  5. research_worker/ -- Dedicated FastAPI worker service (port 8007) that    executes async missions in background threads with Redis pub/sub progress    events and 7-day Redis job persistence.

userNeed.title: System processes pipeline runs within acceptable time limits and scales to multiple organisations
userNeed.description: All users need the system to process pipeline runs within acceptable time limits. A full audit pipeline for a single patient should complete within 2 minutes. The system must scale horizontally to handle multiple organisations running concurrent pipeline jobs. Infrastructure must support auto-scaling based on queue depth and maintain availability of 99.5% during business hours.

userNeed.title: System provides electronic safety-netting for patients with cancer-relevant symptoms
userNeed.description: Pathway coordinators need electronic safety-netting tools that identify patients who presented with cancer-relevant symptoms but were not referred or investigated within expected timeframes. The system shall flag patients where there is a gap between symptom presentation and expected follow-up action, enabling proactive outreach. This supports the Network Contract DES requirement for strengthening and standardising safety netting, including the use of electronic tools.

userNeed.title: Referral management administrators need the system to ingest incoming referrals from all channels into a single unified queue
userNeed.description: Referrals currently arrive through multiple channels. e-RS is the primary NHS channel, but email referrals, posted letters, faxed letters, and in some cases direct EHR-to-EHR referrals also occur. Each channel requires a different monitoring process. Referrals arriving outside e-RS are not automatically visible to the referral management team and can sit undetected in a generic email inbox for days. Even within e-RS, referrals may be directed to wrong mailboxes or departments. The system must provide adapters for each major referral channel that extract the referral content, normalise it to a standard internal format, and place it in the unified queue within a defined time limit from arrival. Channel of origin must be recorded with every referral for audit purposes.

userNeed.title: System imports patient records via FHIR R4 and exports audit results as FHIR resources
userNeed.description: System administrators need the system to import patient encounter records via FHIR R4 APIs (Encounter, DocumentReference, Patient resources) from GP clinical systems. The system must also export audit results as FHIR resources including Measure (audit programme definitions), MeasureReport (programme results), and Device (system identity). FHIR compliance enables integration with NHS Digital infrastructure and interoperability with other audit tools.

userNeed.title: Audit and coding staff see every task they need to action in one unified queue
userNeed.description: Audit and coding staff today open at least five screens to do a full day work: the coding-review queue, the safety-net alerts list, the gold-label review queue, the surface-form review queue, and the audit-run inbox. They tell us the commonest question at stand-up is where do I pick up from yesterday. The user need: a single /work route that, for the staff role, is the app landing page. It lists every open task the user is responsible for, grouped by task type but displayed as one ordered queue. Each row says what the task is, why it is urgent, and which action resolves it. Filters let staff focus on a specific source (coding, safety, gold) without losing visibility of the others.
